title: fix : copper polygons and their cutouts
description: Fixes the issue where copper geometry is lost in polygon-cutout cases, ensuring linked cutouts are retained and properly exported as BREP inner rings.
body: ## Motivation The converter loses copper geometry in two polygon-cutout cases. A linked cutout can suppress a polygon with no poured-copper region. On the [MIT-licensed CH582 board](https://github.com/iot-lorawan/CH582_PCB_SCH/blob/b65bce802295c6c40413c5bc3ea54682820619c1/PCB_ch582_2022-06-16.pcbdoc), two polygons survive, but their four unlinked cutouts are missing from the exported pours. # Reference ## Changes - Suppress a polygon only when a linked `COPPER` region supplies its poured geometry; retain linked cutouts as inner rings. - Resolve linked polygon references by record, including explicit IDs; dangling references do not become inferred holes. - Match unlinked, fully enclosed cutouts to polygons by copper layer and contour geometry, then export those cutouts as BREP inner rings. Cutouts that are not fully enclosed are not inferred as holes. - Reject boundary-touching cutouts as BREP inner holes, with concave-polygon and fractional-mil regressions. - Subtract the combined cutout geometry with `polygon-clipping` before emitting copper. Overlapping and duplicate cutouts remain empty, and a copper island is clipped if another cutout covers it; all three cases have regressions. - Check cutouts on both CH582 copper layers, with a bottom-copper snapshot and an all-layer PCB snapshot. The Circuit JSON renderings show the cutout openings. - Assert that CH582 bottom-layer tracks also survive conversion as Circuit JSON traces. - Keep the small linked-cutout regression and the check that poured-copper regions do not duplicate polygons. [CH582 before, bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/altium-to-circuit-json/2d855de/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts.snap.svg) · [after, bottom copper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/altium-to-circuit-json/8d11a62e391957c94146f762f624472606c69cb0/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts.snap.svg) · [after, all-layer PCB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/altium-to-circuit-json/8d11a62e391957c94146f762f624472606c69cb0/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts-board.snap.svg) The source panels are rendered by `altiumts`, not Altium's official viewer. The Circuit JSON panels use `circuit-to-svg`, which [masks trace strokes covered by a finalized pour](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/blob/main/lib/pcb/copper-pour-trace-mask.ts). That is why bottom routes visible in the source panel are not visible in the rendered Circuit JSON panel; they are present in the converted Circuit JSON. The pre-fix reproduction was merged in #95.

title: Preserve rich line and arc component bodies
description: Recognizes complex custom schematic bodies built from any two supported primitive families and preserves specific transformer and MOSFET graphics while updating affected SVG snapshots for review.
body:
## Summary

- recognize complex custom schematic bodies built from any two supported primitive families
- preserve the LM5155EVM-FLY transformer and optocoupler graphics
- preserve the LM251772EVM-PD detailed MOSFET graphics while keeping ordinary rectangular ICs on the generic-box path
- update every affected side-by-side Altium/Circuit JSON SVG snapshot so the full visual impact is reviewable

## Root cause

Custom bodies were accepted only when they simultaneously contained an ellipse, an elliptical arc, and a polygon. Valid Altium symbols commonly use different combinations such as arcs plus polylines, lines plus polygons, or lines plus ellipses, so they silently degraded into generic boxes.

The new predicate requires at least three body primitives across at least two primitive kinds. This keeps sparse decoration on the generic-box path without requiring one arbitrary combination of shapes.

## Stack

This is stacked on #135 so multipart logic-gate recognition remains a separate root fix and its SVG changes are reviewed there.

## Verification

- 62 targeted SVG tests across the affected existing snapshot files — 62 pass

title: Preserve custom and multipart logic-gate bodies
description: Preserves custom single-input triangular gate bodies instead of degrading them to generic boxes, keeps primitive gate pins, inversion bubbles, clock markers, active-low overbars, and source font sizing aligned with the imported geometry, normalizes only numeric multipart prefixes for gate classification, while retaining original labels such as 1A, 1Y, 2A, and 2Y, preserves both the two-input and Schmitt-trigger gate bodies in TI LMG342X-BB-EVM; power-only multipart sections remain ordinary boxes, includes focused semantic tests and side-by-side AltiumCircuit JSON SVG regressions.
body:
## Summary

- preserve custom single-input triangular gate bodies instead of degrading them to generic boxes
- keep primitive gate pins, inversion bubbles, clock markers, active-low overbars, and source font sizing aligned with the imported geometry
- normalize only numeric multipart prefixes for gate classification, while retaining original labels such as `1A`, `1Y`, `2A`, and `2Y`
- preserve both the two-input and Schmitt-trigger gate bodies in TI LMG342X-BB-EVM; power-only multipart sections remain ordinary boxes
- include focused semantic tests and side-by-side Altium/Circuit JSON SVG regressions

## Root cause

Gate recognition expected literal `A`, `B`, and `Y` pin names. Multipart Altium libraries prefix those functional names with their part number (`1A`, `1Y`, and so on), so valid gate primitives were ignored. Single-input triangular gates also required a dedicated primitive rendering path to keep pin-edge graphics and source labels attached.

The classifier now removes a leading numeric part prefix only while deciding gate semantics. It never rewrites the source port label.

## Verification

- `bun test ./tests/conversion` — 148 pass, 1,719 assertions
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- targeted Biome check on changed TypeScript files
- visually inspected the updated LMG342X-BB-EVM side-by-side schematic snapshot

title: Fix Altium PCB dimension axes in TI EVM imports
description: Fixes incorrect PCB dimension measurements by projecting Altium linear dimensions onto their stored ANGLE axis, ensuring accurate rendering and reference points in TI EVM imports.
body:
## Summary

- project Altium linear dimensions onto their stored `ANGLE` axis instead of measuring the diagonal between reference points
- preserve the original second reference anchor with a fabrication-note extension path to the projected measurement endpoint
- derive the axis with `transformation-matrix`, following the repository and handbook convention for rotations
- render solder mask and drill openings in the four newly added TI EVM comparison snapshots so uncovered substrate is not presented as missing board geometry
- refresh the five existing TI PMP snapshots that exercise the corrected dimension behavior

## Root cause

Altium linear dimensions may store reference points that differ along both axes while `ANGLE` identifies the actual measurement axis. Measuring the direct distance between the references produced diagonal dimensions and incorrect labels. Projecting the second endpoint fixed the measurement but discarded where its extension line originated, so the rendered line no longer reached the feature being measured.

The converter now computes the projection once and uses it for both the Circuit JSON dimension and, when the second reference is off-axis, a fabrication-note path from the original anchor to the projected endpoint. Already aligned dimensions do not receive an extra path.

## Verification

- handbook compliance and one-top-level-function source-structure tests
- four focused PCB-dimension conversion tests, including an off-axis second reference and its extension path
- nine TI EVM PCB SVG snapshot tests covering changed and unchanged dimension cases
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`

The earlier complete suite run passed 208 tests. The full TMDS62LEVM PCB render exceeded its existing 600-second test timeout; all 57 TMDS62LEVM schematic sheets passed.

title: Fix drill boundary precision with before/after visual diff
description: Fixes boundary conflict in drill geometry calculations by retrying in micrometers and returning results to millimeters, ensuring accurate copper retention and drill exclusion in PCB designs.
body:
Stacked on #2. Merge the baseline PR first, then this fix.

The baseline adds the reduced smart-ring case and a snapshot of its actual conversion failure. This PR retries the specific FlattenJS boundary conflict in micrometers, returns the result to millimeters, and updates the **same PNG and SVG snapshots**. In Files changed, open `tests/__snapshots__/trace-drill-boundary-precision.snap.png` to compare the images with GitHub's image diff.

The left panel is the unchanged input copper envelope. The right panel changes from the boundary-conflict exception to the correctly drilled copper ring. The 1.7 nm offending segment is inside the via pad and below the image resolution; the caption makes that limit explicit. This is a converter/DRC robustness fix, not a route-placement change.

Validation: all 136 tests pass, including existing visual/raster comparisons; typecheck passes. No pre-existing geometry snapshots change. The geometry regression verifies retained copper, removed drill, expected area, and original coordinate bounds. The original smart-ring build was also checked with this fix: zero runtime errors, with five remaining design diagnostics correctly causing CLI exit 1.

title: Add SysConfig inspection and CC2340 fixture tests
description: Add textual inspection of .syscfg documents and CC2340 pedometer fixture tests to allow review of configuration settings and recorded target headers without executing scripts.
body:
## Purpose
Add textual inspection of `.syscfg` documents and CC2340 pedometer fixture tests so explicit configuration settings and recorded target headers can be reviewed without executing scripts.

## Changes
- Export `inspectSysConfig(config)` with source-ordered rows for modules, instances, assignments, fixed assignments, suggestions, declarations, calls, unknown statements, and recorded `@cliArgs`, `@v2CliArgs`, and `@versions` metadata.
- Retain repeated entries, parsed target spelling, Unicode identifiers, and bracket notation. Inspection leaves source unchanged and does not evaluate aliases, expressions, SDK defaults, or pin solutions.
- Use `toMatchInlineSnapshot()` for clear text expectations in the compact inspection fixture and pedometer header/pin tests.
- Cover all pedometer GPIO/I²C identifiers, the I²C suggestion, BLE/FreeRTOS/NVS/AES settings, omitted defaults, byte-identical round trips, and controlled edits.
- Keep the inspection implementation in `lib/inspection/` with explicit exports, direct TypeScript packaging, and no added dependencies. Document usage in `docs/inspection.md`.
- Run text-based tests in CI without image artifact generation or uploads.

## Fixture provenance and scope
The pedometer fixture is a **documented transcription of the user-supplied configuration**, with Markdown escaping removed and whitespace normalized. It records device `CC2340R5RGE`, package `RGE`, FreeRTOS, `simplelink_lowpower_f3_sdk@9.21.00.36`, and tool `1.26.3+4558`. The board's wiring and exact orderable MPN have not been independently verified. See `tests/fixtures/pedometer/README.md`.

**Real TI generation, firmware compilation, and hardware execution: NOT RUN.** Parser and inspection tests do not establish hardware validity or end-to-end Circuit JSON conversion.

## Validation
Local checks for head `5fc8117c07e07d9265cc008cedc90d4d8f271003`:
- `bun test`: **40 passed, 0 failed**, including **2 inline snapshots** across 3 test files.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run format:check`: **passed**.
- Unicode targets, bracket-path distinctions, metadata ordering, exact source preservation, deterministic inspection, and unknown source handling remain covered.

GitHub Actions passed for the same head:

body:
Pedometer v0.4.4 uses four pins differently from the supplied development-notes reference. This draft converts the actual board’s source-port identities into three GPIO requests (display isolation DIO20, charger low-power control DIO3, accelerometer input DIO12) and one 100 kbit/s I2C bus (DIO8 SDA / DIO6_A1_AR+ SCL). Display bus/control and SWD ownership is reserved explicitly; SPI and a complete pedometer firmware application are outside this scope.

The staged API now accepts multiple CC2340 GPIOs and an optional I2C request, with explicit firmware choices, exact MPN/package resolution, alias/ownership checks, conflict rejection, deterministic output and input snapshotting. GPIO electrical declarations are accepted when they agree with supported requested settings; contradictory or unsupported declarations fail. The resolved CC2340 target is carried through pin resolution and document generation, including both header versions. The AM2434 single-GPIO API and its existing tests/workflow remain intact.

The public I2C `max_bit_rate` remains in bits/s. The exporter converts 100000 bits/s to the SDK's numeric `maxBitRate = 100` kbit/s; the independent v0.4.4 reference is corrected too. The regression checks numeric values before and after serialization/re-parsing. The historical fixture keeps its original incorrect units unchanged and documents that error separately.

The v0.4.4 source archive, per-file hashes and original generated JSON are frozen in tests/fixtures/pedometer. The supplied reference is preserved byte-for-byte as an unmatched parser fixture. A separately authored v0.4.4 GPIO/I2C reference is present but is NOT yet used as a TI-validated expectation. Detailed provenance, the four conflicting assignments, reproduction commands and status are in [the fixture record](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/blob/add-cc2340-pedometer/tests/fixtures/pedometer/README.md).

Validation completed locally:
- Published tscircuit 0.0.2463 source build exited 0; rebuilding the archived sources reproduced all circuit records except the project filesystem hash.
- 160 tests and 3 inline snapshots passed; typecheck, formatting and git diff checks passed.
- A separate TSX regression circuit was rebuilt after changing pin5/DIO12 to pin6/DIO13; unchanged converter options follow the regenerated physical pin. The frozen pedometer was not modified.
- Real AM2434 native, round-trip, converted A7 and converted B7 generation/comparisons passed using SysConfig 1.14.0+2667 and SDK e7e068494bbd5714d6d34c55b10184a5bd84ed30.

**The existing green TI SysConfig validation check covers AM2434 only. It is not evidence of CC2340 acceptance.**

**Draft blockers / NOT RUN:**
- Separate approval is pending for SysConfig 1.26.3+4558 and SimpleLink F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 (official SDK revision c55fa9bae0ec71b103508afac4861d446204669b). CC2340 TI generation has NOT RUN.
- Independently validate the new reference, round-trip, converter output and changed-pin cases. Inspect actual SimpleLink output for pins, GPIO electrical settings, I2C assignments, no unexpected display/debug allocations, `CONFIG_I2C_0_MAXSPEED = 100U`, and `CONFIG_I2C_0_MAXBITRATE = I2C_100kHz`; reject `I2C_400kHz`. Implement these strict comparisons and the separate CC2340 CI job. No mocked TI acceptance is claimed.
- BLE/FreeRTOS/NVS application-preset reuse is deferred pending compatibility/resource checks. This draft explicitly selects NoRTOS and copies no historical application settings.
- GUI loading, CC2340 pin-change TI execution, firmware compilation and hardware execution remain unverified.

Do not merge until the real CC2340 validation work is completed.

body:
Adds a dedicated GitHub Actions check for real TI generation, following the local validation completed in #2. Every pull request and push to main runs the unchanged `bun run validate:ti` runner for native, round-trip, converted A7, and converted B7 inputs. Manual dispatch is also available.

Bash pipefail preserves validation failures while saving output. Setup logs, versions, validation output, and all generated files are uploaded as a 14-day Actions artifact even on failure.

No secrets, converter changes, or relaxed assertions. The README documents unattended TI-license acceptance and reproduction.

### Validation

- **Real Linux CI passed:** [TI validation run](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36636274455) on head `6b9f58fdfe5de79fcfbbc7f214bc563c11ab35d7` (GitHub test merge `56741831a7f40b72163e34232150bba3fe4937ee`), Ubuntu 22.04.5 x86_64; job completed in 40 seconds.

- Converted A7: MCU_GPIO0_5 / MCU_SPI1_CS0; converted B7: MCU_GPIO0_6 / MCU_SPI1_CS1. Both output direction, mode 7, exactly one MCU-domain pin and no extra reservations.
- [Uploaded evidence](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36636274455/artifacts/11065430067) downloaded and verified: logs plus all four fresh inputs and 20 generated files per case.
- [Tests](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36636274401), [typecheck](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36636274419), and [format](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36636274520) passed on the same head.

Firmware compilation and hardware execution remain outside this check. This adds a CI check; repository branch-protection settings are unchanged.

title: Add TI-validated Circuit JSON → SysConfig GPIO conversion for AM2434
description: Circuit JSON now produces a single GPIO SysConfig document for AM2434BSDFHIALVR. A source-port ball alias A7 fixes the output to MCU_GPIO0_5; changing that alias to B7 fixes it to MCU_GPIO0_6. Unknown parts, ambiguous identities, ownership errors, and unsupported active functions fail explicitly.
body:
Circuit JSON now produces a single GPIO SysConfig document for **AM2434BSDFHIALVR**. A source-port ball alias A7 fixes the output to MCU_GPIO0_5; changing that alias to B7 fixes it to MCU_GPIO0_6. Unknown parts, ambiguous identities, ownership errors, and unsupported active functions fail explicitly.

### Implementation

- Public `CircuitJsonToSysConfigConverter` with three concrete stages: resolve MCU/target, validate GPIO, construct the document. `step()` performs one stage; `runUntilFinished()` completes the remaining stages; `getOutput()` rejects unfinished conversion. Failed stages do not advance, completed steps do not duplicate output, and inputs are snapshotted.
- The convenience function is a thin wrapper over the same converter. Shared context carries the selected component/port, resolved target/request, and document; the GPIO resolver uses that resolved target.
- Pins the merged sysconfigts commit **`35381191fb3946185632d9c4c2ac4c2e69329535`** from [sysconfigts #1](https://github.com/tscircuit/sysconfigts/pull/1). Consumer tests use `inspectSysConfig()` with reviewed inline snapshots, including fixed versus suggested assignments, determinism, non-mutation, and serialization/re-parsing. Obsolete SVG consumer tests and references are removed.
- Rejects non-string `gpio_name` values before identifier matching. Physical labels use the verified ALV 21×21 package grid: `CS1` remains a signal alias, while real unsupported balls still trigger ambiguity checks.
- The existing TI runner reads actual main/MCU pinmux initializer entries, excluding `PINMUX_END`. It rejects unannotated extras, duplicate reservations, and unknown initializer forms, comparing converted output with independently specified expectations.
- The native TI fixture is unchanged. Debug UART allocation remains disabled. No new target/peripheral support, renderer, CLI, build, or publishing machinery.

### Target provenance

Exact MPN/package: [TI orderable-part page](https://www.ti.com/product/AM2434/part-details/AM2434BSDFHIALVR). [AM243x datasheet SPRSP65J](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/am2434.pdf), Tables 5-1/5-42, verifies A7 → MCU_SPI1_CS0 / MCU_GPIO0_5 and B7 → MCU_SPI1_CS1 / MCU_GPIO0_6, both mode 7. Package drawing ALV0441A / 4225999/A documents the complete ball grid.

SysConfig device `AM243x_ALV_beta`, package/part `ALV`, core `r5fss0-0`; required tool **1.14.0+2667**. SDK source tag `REL.MCUSDK.08.06.00.34`, commit `e7e068494bbd5714d6d34c55b10184a5bd84ed30`; its [manifest](https://github.com/TexasInstruments/mcupsdk-core/blob/e7e068494bbd5714d6d34c55b10184a5bd84ed30/.metadata/product.json) retains `MCU_PLUS_SDK@07.03.01`. Full source/license references ship in `lib/targets/README.md`.

### Validation at d3583a2245be6ea1ce0cb27df0d4138768ed70b2

- `bun install --verbose`: passed; ordinary `bun install` stalled during resolution and was interrupted before retrying with diagnostics. No dependency or lockfile workaround.
- `bun test`: **127 pass, 0 fail; 2 reviewed inline snapshots**.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `git diff --check`: passed.
- GitHub Actions on this commit: [tests](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36626409097), [typecheck](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36626409086), and [format](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/actions/runs/36626409126) all passed.
- All README TypeScript examples executed successfully; native fixture SHA-256 unchanged.
- `bun run validate:ti`: **PASSED, exit 0** with the actual TI engine; all four inputs passed. No implementation or validation assertions changed.

### Real TI execution — PASSED (2026-09-29)

title: Add CAD collision error schema
description: Add a CAD collision error schema to record mechanical collisions in Circuit JSON, including affected references and area measurements.
body:
An enclosure aperture can be visibly misplaced while Circuit JSON has no mechanical collision error record to describe the collision. Add `cad_collision_error` with the affected CAD/PCB/source references, enclosure CAD IDs, resolved face, measured area, and threshold.

The area is the union silhouette of the actual solid intersection projected along the aperture face normal, in mm². It is neither volume nor total mesh surface area. The diagnostic indicates a possible aperture position/size or body-clearance problem.

- Export the Zod schema, input/output types, and `AnyCircuitElement` union member.
- Reject non-finite/negative areas, invalid faces, and empty enclosure references.

title: Fix VBUS power pin inference
description: Fixes the incorrect classification of the VBUS power pin in the USB hub board, eliminating misleading missing-power warnings for components connected to VBUS.
body:
## Motivation

The [USB hub board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/usb-hub-board) uses five [USBLC6-2SC6 components](https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/USBLC6-2SC6/C2687116). Their imported pin 5 is correctly labeled `VBUS`, but the converter does not classify that exact label as a power pin.

As a result, tscircuit emits misleading missing-power warnings for U3 and U9 through U12 even though each component has a VBUS connection.

Reproduction: #577

## Fix

Treat exact `VBUS` labels, including numbered forms such as `VBUS2`, like the existing `VCC`, `VDD`, and `VIN` power labels. The existing ambiguity guard remains unchanged, so mixed-function aliases such as `VBUS` plus `IO` are not automatically classified.

## Before and after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| VBUS is only a label, so the component reports no power pin. | VBUS receives power metadata and the misleading warning disappears. |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/easyeda-converter/5e951f1e859474a4a296096ca35bb65fd7c1c56b/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C2687116-vbus-power-metadata-repro.snap.svg) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/135313b2a79d79a3632d3dacf2c21ff0f3e17e01/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C2687116-vbus-power-metadata-repro.snap.svg) |

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/infer-pin-attributes.test.ts tests/convert-to-ts/C2687116-to-ts.test.ts tests/convert-to-ts/C7203002-to-ts.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`

The focused USBLC6-2SC6 regression, general inference tests, and the existing Raspberry Pi Pico VBUS case all pass.

## Motivation

[USB hub board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/usb-hub-board) uses five USBLC6-2SC6 protection chips imported from JLCPCB part C2687116. Each imported chip exposes pin 5 as VBUS, but the generated pin attributes only classify GND.

This leaves the VBUS source port without `requires_power` and produces five misleading missing-power warnings on the real board: U3 and U9 through U12.

## Evidence

| Source | Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JLCPCB / EasyEDA | [Exact C2687116 source fixture](https://github.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/blob/repro-vbus-power-pin-inference/tests/assets/C2687116.raweasy.json) | Pin 5 is labeled `VBUS` |
| tscircuit import | [Generated schematic snapshot](https://github.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/blob/repro-vbus-power-pin-inference/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C2687116-vbus-power-metadata-repro.snap.svg) | `VBUS` is preserved as the pin label |
| Circuit JSON | Focused assertions in the reproduction test | VBUS has no `requires_power` and a `source_no_power_pin_defined_warning` is emitted |

![C2687116 imported schematic snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/repro-vbus-power-pin-inference/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C2687116-vbus-power-metadata-repro.snap.svg)

## Reproduction

| Stage | Current output |
| --- | --- |
| EasyEDA pin | pin 5 is labeled `VBUS` |
| Generated TSX | `pin5` contains `VBUS`, without `requiresPower` |
| Circuit JSON | VBUS source port has no `requires_power` |
| Diagnostic | Missing-power warning is emitted |

This PR adds the exact C2687116 EasyEDA fixture, a generated tscircuit schematic snapshot, and a focused regression test that captures the current behavior. It does not change converter logic, so there is no after snapshot in this reproduction-only PR.

title: Fix enclosure resource cleanup and unnecessary PCB texture rebuilds
description: Fixes resource cleanup for enclosures and prevents unnecessary PCB texture regeneration when changing visibility states.
body:
Switching an enclosure between opaque and translucent currently rebuilds its JSCAD geometry. Changing CAD visibility also regenerates PCB textures in both the JSCAD and Manifold renderers, and unmounted JSCAD models leave their geometry and material undisposed.

This change keeps geometry tied to the JSCAD plan, updates transparency on the existing material, and disposes resources on plan replacement or unmount (including React StrictMode replay). PCB texture caching now depends only on the layer visibility flags that affect those textures. Texture resolution, lighting, and mechanical geometry are preserved.

Validation:
- Five new regression tests cover geometry reuse, disposal, StrictMode/plan replacement, and texture invalidation in both renderers. The existing Manifold StrictMode test also passes (6/6 targeted tests).
- `tsc --noEmit` and `bun run build` pass.
- Full suite: 153 pass, 6 fail. Unmodified current `main`: 148 pass, the same 6 fail. The existing failures cover orientation-canvas StrictMode replay, faux-board Z offsets, and 3D-to-SVG conversion.

These fixes address reproduced allocation and cache invalidation bugs; this PR does not claim to establish the cause of a reported browser crash or sustained orbit lag.

title: repro: existing trace obstacles omit copper width and end caps
description: Fixes obstacle generation for autorouting by ensuring that PCB traces are fully represented, including their width and end caps, preventing routing overlaps.
body:
Existing PCB traces are not fully represented as obstacles for the autorouter. When `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` converts a trace, it drops the actual wire width, and `getObstaclesFromRoute` uses a fixed 0.1 mm thickness and stops at the centerline endpoints. For example, a 10 mm long, 0.5 mm wide trace becomes a 10 × 0.1 mm obstacle instead of covering the full copper area, including its rounded ends. This leaves real copper outside the obstacle and can allow new routes too close to, or overlapping, existing traces. The printed-coil circuit below reproduces the incorrect obstacle dimensions.

Motive: Ensure routing obstacles cover all existing copper so new routes can avoid it correctly.

![Printed-coil sensor PCB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrithik18k/core/repro/wide-trace-obstacle-coverage/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-wide-trace-obstacle-snapshot-pcb.snap.svg)

body:
`<autoroutingphase autorouter="bus_lanes" />` now routes the AM3352/RAM fixture from TSX, with local pad-to-via dogbones when a layer transition is needed. Existing fanout exits are used directly. The fixture contains no custom algorithm and no saved route geometry.

The solver preserves single-layer carriers, bus length matching, coupled differential pairs, curved tuning, and reduced unnecessary turns. The regression requires all 47 traces and zero errors, and checks pair gap/skew, bus skew, layer transitions, detour and turn limits. Only fully routed snapshots are included.

title: Fix portable bus routing and remove the ARM-only snapshot job
description: Fixes routing calculation for AM3352 by removing the ARM-only snapshot job and reverting to normal test shards on ubuntu-latest.
body:
AM3352 routing snapshots currently require a dedicated ARM runner because native `Math.hypot` rounding changes equal-length shortcut choices on x86. [bus-lanes-solver #6](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/6) fixes the routing-distance calculation and includes a regression that fails on x86 before the fix.

Use the released solver 0.0.3 from jscdn and return AM3352 to the normal `ubuntu-latest` test shards. Remove the dedicated ARM job and the shard exclusion. The TSX fixture, three routed snapshots, 169 assertions, DRC gates, and zero image-diff tolerance are unchanged.

Validation: all ten regular x86 test shards, formatting, smoke test, and deployment checks are green ([CI run](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/36782627264)). The AM3352 shard passed in 11m48s with the existing snapshots and all routing assertions unchanged. Full AM3352 also passes on ARM with 47/47 signals and zero native errors; six focused bus_lanes integration tests and the packaged dist build/smoke test pass.

This PR targets the integration branch from merged #4237 (parent #4232 is still open) to keep the diff to two files. Solver #6 is merged; the dependency now points to https://jscdn.tscircuit.com/@tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/0.0.3.tgz. Its JavaScript bundle and TypeScript declarations are byte-identical to the preview validated above. Installation and all six focused bus_lanes tests pass with the released tarball.

description: Updates the package dependencies to use compact published routing packages instead of larger npm packages, ensuring fresh installs exclude former runtime dependencies.
body:
Use the compact published routing packages instead of a bus-lanes Git checkout and the larger schematic solver npm package. Update connectivity-map to ^1.0.1 so fresh installs exclude its former Biome runtime dependency.

- Pin bus-lanes-solver 0.0.2 and schematic-trace-solver 0.0.215 to their versioned jscdn tarballs (approximately 1.13 MiB and 0.84 MiB unpacked).
- Preserve the existing bundling configuration and solver interfaces. This repository intentionally disables saving Bun lockfiles.

Validation: build including declarations, TypeScript check, built-distribution smoke test, and 7 focused bus-routing/schematic connectivity tests passed (42 assertions). Installed package versions and absence of runtime dependencies on both solver tarballs were verified.

Merge and release core before the corresponding eval/tscircuit dependency updates: their copy-core-versions scripts otherwise restore the older references from the currently published core.

title: Route all 47 AM3352 signals with the public bus_lanes phase
description: The original AM3352RAM board now routes all 47 signals with zero native DRC errors through the public phase. The fixture preserves the reference TSXs footprints, placement, 47 connections, two byte buses, three differential pairs, and timing constraints. It contains no custom algorithm or saved route plan. Automatic dogbones apply only to untouched component pads; existing fanout handoffs stay fixed.
body:
The original [AM3352/RAM board](https://tscircuit.com/seveibar/am3352-ram-dogbone-and-single-layer-route-test) now routes all **47 signals with zero native DRC errors** through the public phase:

```tsx
<autoroutingphase name="DDR_BUS_LANES" phaseIndex={1} autorouter="bus_lanes" />
```

The fixture preserves the reference TSX's footprints, placement, 47 connections, two byte buses, three differential pairs, and timing constraints. It contains no custom algorithm or saved route plan. Automatic dogbones apply only to untouched component pads; existing fanout handoffs stay fixed.

![Completed AM3352 signal layers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/7affa9d1b6fff327c17f957981a300695d91a7a2/docs/routed-am3352/solved.png)

Start review with `tests/features/autorouter-bus-lanes-am3352.test.tsx` and its three signal-layer SVG snapshots. Every snapshot is written only after these gates pass:
- 47 distinct routes, zero native circuit errors, exactly two local vias per signal, and a single-layer via-free carrier.
- 1549.71 mm total copper (limit 1700); maximum/mean detour 2.047/1.546 (limits 2.6/1.75).
- 540 ordinary turns and 145 short jogs (limits 900/460), with zero acute corners.
- Byte skew ≤0.635 mm; pair skew ≤0.127 mm, including fixed dogbones.
- Pair interior edge gaps 0.11213–0.13813 mm, inside the unchanged 0.0999–0.155 mm limits and 6.2 mm per-end approach allowance.

The source-bus assertion includes both byte buses and all three exported differential-pair memberships. The snapshot views explicitly select inner1, inner2, and bottom so the carrier routing is visible. No partial/unrouted AM3352 artifacts are included.

Validation: fresh TSX integration run passed in 281 seconds with 169 assertions; six smaller bus_lanes integration tests and core typecheck pass. The test timeout is 900 seconds for this dense regression. The solver has 49 passing tests and four passing DDR benchmarks; see [solver #3](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/3).

**Dependencies:** props uses the built, commit-pinned PR preview from [props #875](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/875) in both devDependencies and overrides. Replace this preview with its npm release before merge. The dist build and smoke test pass from a clean CI install. The dense AM3352 test has a dedicated Ubuntu ARM job matching the snapshot-update runner, with all 169 assertions and zero image-diff tolerance. Other tests continue in the ten x86 shards. ARM and x86 can select different valid control paths due to floating-point geometry differences. The tested solver is pinned to `de425372f6413e024010d24b64341d64c83a6a12`, which uses [fanout-solver #252](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/252). This PR is stacked on [planning #4232](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4232).




CI is green on `fa67b539ed24f804820a4e8af5172d5b81a9bf92`: all ten x86 test shards, the dedicated AM3352 ARM routing/snapshot job (169 assertions), dist build/smoke test, and Vercel preview pass. [Test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/36779502812). No routing assertions, DRC gates, image tolerances, or snapshot geometry were weakened or changed.

title: Fix dogbone phase artifact export and fanout-local coordinates
description: Fixes export issues with dogbone phase artifacts by selecting only physical ports as export anchors and using the owning fanout group for local coordinates, ensuring proper PCB trace path imports.
body:
Dogbone phase artifacts currently cannot be saved by the CLI: their provisional fanout exits coincide with source pads, so the exporter reports an ambiguous endpoint. When the fanout is moved, exported coordinates also use the enclosing board frame instead of the fanout's local frame.

Select only physical ports as export anchors and use the owning fanout group for local coordinates. This makes emitted `pcbTracePaths` importable on the same `<fanout autorouter="dogbone" />`, including connected VCC/GND pads.

Regression coverage exports, edits widths, and replays the paths at a translated fanout across both board sides and all four right-angle rotations, checking identical copper positions and no circuit errors, with eight visual snapshots.

Validation: TypeScript check; breakout suite; CLI end-to-end build → JSON artifact → edited width/bend → saved fanout rebuild using this built core. Follow-up to #4235.

title: Add dogbone fanout using the published dogbone-solver package
description: Enable fanout autorouting using the dogbone algorithm for SMT pads to nearby vias without routing to the fanout boundary.
body:
Enable `<fanout autorouter="dogbone">` using the published standalone [`@tscircuit/dogbone-solver`](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver) package. Core bundles the exact [jscdn 0.0.1 release](https://jscdn.tscircuit.com/@tscircuit/dogbone-solver/0.0.1.tgz).

```tsx
<fanout autorouter="dogbone">
  <AM3352 />
</fanout>
```

The algorithm, asynchronous SRJ adapter, BaseSolver implementation, Cosmos debugger and algorithm visual tests live in the new solver repository, merged in https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/pull/1. Core only registers the preset/solver, prepares fanout connectivity, preserves completed copper, and synchronizes solved handoffs through the existing routing pipeline. No custom algorithm function, solver input field or completion callback is attached to the phase plan.

The same strategy works with `<autoroutingphase autorouter="dogbone" />` and the standard follow-up router. It receives the current phase SRJ, runs asynchronously, emits solver/debug events, and passes the updated SRJ onward.

The AM3352 test stays declarative TSX and a labeled snapshot: 324 local escapes, including 43 VSS and 76 supply/capacitor-related pads. Core integration regressions cover transformed footprints, async lifecycle/replay/cancellation, failure handling and downstream via connections. Standalone solver algorithm tests and debugger pages are in dogbone-solver.

Validation: installed the versioned jscdn tarball; all 32 breakout tests pass (two existing skips); TypeScript typecheck, distribution build and distribution smoke test pass. Solver repo CI passes all five tests, typechecking and formatting; its Cosmos export builds. SVG snapshots were rendered and inspected. Interactive localhost browser inspection was blocked by a saved browser permission.

![AM3352 local dogbones](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/test/am3352-dogbone-all-pads/tests/breakout/__snapshots__/fanout-am3352-dogbones-pcb.snap.svg)

title: feat: add regulator capacitor and pull-resistor placement warnings
description: Enables RegulatorCapacitorsOnWrongSides and PullResistorOnWrongSide in the schematic checks, providing warnings for incorrect placement of regulator capacitors and pull resistors in schematics.
body:
Enables `RegulatorCapacitorsOnWrongSides` and `PullResistorOnWrongSide` in the schematic checks. Regulator warnings identify input/output capacitors placed across the regulator from their connected pins; pull-resistor warnings identify pull-ups below their signal pin or pull-downs above it. Both preserve component, port, sheet, and subcircuit associations.

Validation: all 584 tests, typecheck, build, and formatting pass. TSX tests cover both check entry points, corrected placement, sheet isolation, and stable warning IDs. The existing unchanged ESP32 and F1C1990S repros produce one and two regulator warnings respectively.

title: test: reproduce missed MPU-6050 via-to-pad clearance
description: Reproduces a bug where the MPU-6050 mini boards V3V3 via is too close to the C3 GND pad, highlighting a clearance issue without changing the checker functionality.
body:
## Issue

A fresh render of the MPU-6050 mini board places a V3V3 via 0.097261 mm from C3 pin 2 (GND). The board requires 0.1 mm pad edge clearance, yet routing DRC reports no clearance error. The via and pad are on different nets and both occupy the top copper layer.

`checkViaPadClearance` currently skips the pair because it adds a 0.005 mm `EPSILON` before comparing the measured gap with the required clearance. Whether that tolerance should apply to a stated 0.1 mm rule is the decision this repro is intended to surface.

## Repro

- Add the Circuit JSON exported from the complete board using `tscircuit@0.0.2565`, with its actual routed via and C3 pad.
- Identify C3 pin 2 through its source component, source port, PCB port, and pad IDs. Verify that it is GND and that the via is V3V3.
- Calculate the circle-to-rectangle gap independently of the checker's geometry helper and snapshot the complete PCB with the measured gap labeled.
- Keep fixture, checker execution, and snapshot checks in a normal test. A separate `test.failing` expects the one missing clearance error, so a render or fixture failure cannot make that assertion appear to pass.

This PR is a reproduction only; it does not change the checker.

Tests were not run, as requested.

title: Skip distant segments in PCB connectivity checks
description: Reduces the time taken for PCB connectivity checks by skipping distant segments, improving performance without affecting design rule checks.
body:
PCB connectivity checks compared every same-layer segment pair with the exact distance predicate, including segments far apart. Reject disjoint expanded bounding boxes first, keeping the continuous contact check and tangent contacts unchanged.

On the fully routed 47-trace AM3352/RAM board, constructing the connectivity map drops from 1.31 s to 0.38 s with identical connected-trace sets. This reduces overhead in the SVG build without skipping DRC.

Validation: 24 tests / 4,091 assertions pass; typecheck and build pass. Added randomized equivalence checks, degenerate segments, translated geometry, and contacts just below/at/above the copper-width threshold.

title: Make datasheet pins easier to scan and expose electrical attributes
description: Replaces long manufacturer notes in datasheet pages with compact, searchable rows that display primary signals, alternate functions, serial capabilities, and electrical requirements, while retaining full notes in per-pin details.
body:
Datasheet pages such as STM8L151K6T6 currently repeat long manufacturer notes in every row, concatenate pin aliases, and omit the stored pin attributes. Replace that table with compact, searchable rows that show a primary signal, separated alternate functions, readable serial capabilities, and explicit electrical requirements. Full notes and every structured attribute remain available in per-pin details.

Electrical summaries use the existing tscircuit/props attributes, without guessing supply voltages or active mux configurations from names or prose. Legacy string names, missing attributes, numeric pin keys, and BGA coordinates remain supported. Narrow layouts keep the details button visible and put electrical information beneath the signal. Overview and source documents share a row on desktop.

Validation:
- `bun test bun-tests/lib/datasheet-pin-display.test.tsx`: 6 tests, 27 assertions passed, including zero voltage, false flags, legacy records, and initially collapsed notes.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run lint` passed.
- Browser checked against the real STM8L151K6T6 API response: 32 pins, notes/capability search, expansion/collapse, empty results, and narrow layout without page overflow.

Full datasheet PDF URLs remain visible and clickable in Source documents, with wrapping for narrow screens. No dependencies added.

body:
Adds an Optical Sensors category to the homepage with `/optical_sensors/list` and `/optical_sensors/list.json`. Optical motion/navigation sensors are recognized by part family or description across mixed upstream categories, including mouse, trackball, and optical flow sensors; dedicated light/interrupter categories are also included. Package, sensor type, basic, and preferred filters let users narrow the results.

Registers the derived table, D1 schema/indexes, database types, and production sync so the category can be populated after merge. Optional missing or malformed metadata does not hide known sensors, and lens accessories and unrelated components are excluded.

Validation: 398 Bun tests and 168 Cloudflare worker tests pass, including source-db-v2 import, schema parity/idempotency, category selection, homepage rendering, and filtered HTML/JSON route coverage. Both TypeScript checks, Biome formatting, shell syntax, and diff whitespace checks pass.

title: Keep recovery builds fast and support all-category runs
description: Optimizes recovery builds by replacing metadata materialization with indexed lookups and adjusts batch sizes for uploads, ensuring faster execution and maintaining data integrity.
body:
Recovery joined a UNION ALL metadata view, causing SQLite to materialize the entire LCSC metadata set for every derived-table batch. Direct joins now use the current and recovery tables' primary-key indexes, with the current record taking precedence exactly as before.

Validation: query plans confirm indexed lookups replace metadata materialization. A real recovered catalog/stock/Ethernet build completed in 61.65 seconds locally and passed integrity_check, yielding the same 732,252 catalog rows and 86 derived Ethernet rows as the previous build before live refresh. All nine source-build tests pass, including current versus recovered manufacturer/attribute precedence, explicit removals, and source preservation. TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks pass.

This follow-up keeps the broader recovery within the workflow time budget. The initial recovery jobs were cancelled during preparation, before production uploads; the validated branch is being used for the manual recovery runs.


All-category runs also hash the requested table list for the prepared-database cache key. The full list is 681 characters before the rest of the key, exceeding the cache action key limit; a SHA-256 digest keeps the key bounded while preserving table-set identity. Workflow YAML parsing and diff checks pass.


Category recovery uploads also use 1,000-row batches, matching the existing full-catalog batch size and reducing D1 command overhead fourfold versus 250-row batches. The existing retry-safe file import path is unchanged.

title: Recover missing upstream catalog parts and refresh Ethernet controllers
description: Restores missing Ethernet controller parts from a previous archive and updates their stock and prices from JLCPCB, ensuring data integrity and validation throughout the process.
body:
The current jlcparts archive lost older parts during its September 14 cache reset, leaving W5500 and ENC28J60 absent from jlcsearch. This change fills missing IDs from the last complete archive and refreshes Ethernet controller stock and prices directly from JLCPCB.

Recovery uses commit `75daa67a78f3acf4ce18bab8dd68a86ac28c2818`, with every archive volume verified against pinned Git blob hashes and sizes. Current upstream records, including explicit removals and zero stock, take precedence. The fallback feeds derived tables, global catalog/search, and stock snapshots so later syncs preserve recovered records. Workflow dispatch exposes an opt-out, and prepared-cache keys include that choice.

The live Ethernet refresh validates all pages before replacing data, updates matching catalog/stock rows, runs on prepared-cache hits, and uploads the category during catalog and nightly stock syncs. Post-upload checks require W5500/ENC28J60 and compare stocked API rows plus HTML/package caches. No README changes.

Validation: all 392 repository tests passed before the final source-preservation guard; all 14 focused recovery/refresh tests passed afterward. Root and worker TypeScript checks, formatting, workflow YAML parsing, and diff checks passed. The actual 13-volume archive passed checksum verification and SQLite quick_check; a real recovered preparation passed integrity_check. Local catalog coverage increased from 52,614 to 732,343 eligible records. JLCPCB returned 190 Ethernet controllers, 91 stocked; W5500 C32843 had 15,926 units, ENC28J60-I/SO C47351 414, and ENC28J60-I/SS C411626 486, consistently reflected in the category, catalog, and stock snapshot.

Operational limits: recovery restores coverage, not universally current stock/prices. Individual fallback records can be months old, although Ethernet data is refreshed live. The archive adds about 680 MB compressed and 5.94 GB extracted during preparation. Production is unchanged by this PR.

Manual rollout: after merge, dispatch Build and Sync D1 with `sync_scope=full_catalog` and `recover_missing_parts=true`; then dispatch `sync_scope=derived` for the other category tables that should be restored. See `docs/source-cache-recovery.md` for details. The full-catalog run uploads refreshed Ethernet data itself; other category tables require the derived run.

body:
`tsci import` leaves out electrical attributes stored in the datasheet API, including the F1C100S AVCC pin's 2.8 V requirement and the AP2127K-2.8TRG1 regulator's 2.8 V output.

Look up the imported component's exact manufacturer part number through the configured registry's datasheet endpoint, validate the returned attributes with the existing props schema, and put them on Circuit JSON source ports. Generate the enriched component with released `circuit-json-to-tscircuit@0.0.50`, which now emits `pinAttributes` directly. This uses the live API and does not depend on parts-engine PR #60. There is no TSX rewrite for pin attributes.

Absent or empty metadata keeps the existing EasyEDA conversion path. Invalid metadata, a mismatched part, failed requests, or the 5-second lookup timeout warn and continue with the existing import. The deadline covers response headers and body; a timeout warns that the datasheet API did not respond within 5 seconds and `pinAttributes` may not be populated. Other lookup failures also warn that attributes may not be populated. Physical pin entries override signal-label entries; existing Circuit JSON fields are preserved. Exact/compact footprints, pin labels, supplier/manufacturer metadata, CAD references, and caller props overrides remain supported.

Use `tsci import C460327 --exclude-pin-attributes` to skip the datasheet lookup and use the existing EasyEDA import path. Importer-inferred attributes (such as ground pins) remain. The flag is covered for both search-result imports and direct part-number fallback.

Only the existing converter devDependency is upgraded; no packages are added.

Validation:
- 20 new tests pass, including all 89 F1C100S pins and five regulator pins in both exact and compact footprint modes, canonical props validation, CAD references, caller overrides, named/physical pin precedence, false/zero values, capabilities, and missing/failing datasheets.
- Typecheck, build, and formatting pass.
- Live CLI imports of C1511928 and C460327 match every attribute in the production datasheet API. Both generated components render with the expected 89/five schematic ports; AVCC requires 2.8 V and regulator pin 5 provides 2.8 V. Rendering these isolated, unwired chips reports only the expected must-be-connected errors.
- The broader local import suite still hits the previously reproduced baseline dependency error: `@tscircuit/props` does not export `assemblySubassemblyProps` for the footprint rendering test. This failure was also reproduced on unchanged main; dependency versions unrelated to the converter are unchanged.

Uses https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/pull/121 and replaces the closed CLI-specific TSX rewrite in https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5063.

title: Preserve silkscreen rectangle rotation and stroke visibility
description: Fixes rendering issues with silkscreen rectangles by preserving their rotation and stroke visibility based on source specifications.
body:
## Motivation

The D7/D8 polarity bars on DRV8307EVM render vertically after the round trip in #89. Their source `pcb_silkscreen_rect` elements specify 270° and 90° rotations, which the converter omits. The source also sets `has_stroke: false`; forwarding its stored stroke width adds an unwanted outline and doubles the bars' visible thickness.

## Before

The generated board on the right has thick vertical yellow bars where the source has thin horizontal bars.

![Before: rectangle rotation and stroke visibility omitted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/ce8d7b0f680215e9a8048a548dd16aade0f0b749/tests/ti-evms/__snapshots__/ti-drv8307evm-roundtrip-pcb-comparison.snap.svg)

## After

Pass `ccw_rotation` to `<silkscreenrect>` using the existing `formatPcbRotationAttr` helper. Emit `strokeWidth={0}` when `has_stroke` is explicitly false, preserving the source width otherwise. D7/D8's polarity bars now match the source orientation and thickness. The converter follows source fields with no board-specific conditions or dimensions.

![After: polarity bar orientation and thickness preserved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/64605c8fb95106269f4b03fe4cced26c1a1fc49c/tests/ti-evms/__snapshots__/ti-drv8307evm-roundtrip-pcb-comparison.snap.svg)

## Validation

- Native round-trip tests cover 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270°, checking rendered width, height, fill, and disabled stroke. The existing stroked rectangle regression also passes.
- Refreshed generated-code and PCB comparison snapshots for all four TI fixtures, preserving the merged via fix.
- Visually checked all four board comparisons.
- `bun test`: 46 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. The same snapshot-summary anomaly appears in the [successful via-fix CI run](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/actions/runs/36835479890), which reports 42 pass, 0 fail and one failed snapshot in its summary.
- Type check, formatting check, and build pass.
- Style follows the [tscircuit handbook](https://github.com/tscircuit/handbook/blob/main/guides/code.md).

Current core correctly renders rectangle quarter-turns by swapping dimensions. Arbitrary-angle rectangle rendering remains a core limitation; this converter forwards the rotation prop without adding a geometry workaround.

title: Preserve board center so imported PCBs fit the full view
description: Fixes rendering issue where imported PCBs were cropped in the viewer due to incorrect board center positioning, ensuring complete visibility of the PCB including original dimensions and scale bars.
body:
## Motivation

Imported TI EVM boards should open with the complete PCB visible, including the original dimension units and scale bars. Boards with coordinates away from the origin were cropped in the viewer, and some side-by-side SVG comparisons also clipped the generated board.

## Before

The converter kept absolute outline and footprint coordinates but omitted `pcb_board.center`. The generated board defaulted to the origin, so the viewer fitted the wrong bounds.

PCB comparisons also normalized SVG dimensions without scaling drawings when the SVG had no `viewBox`, clipping the right and bottom edges of the DRV8307 and LM251772 renders.

![Before: DRV8307 source and generated PCB comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/47cdc0185b792a531c50bf7ea0e56a1532c2629f/tests/ti-evms/__snapshots__/ti-drv8307evm-roundtrip-pcb-comparison.snap.svg)

## After

Use the source board center as `boardAnchorPosition` when an explicit anchor is absent. Footprint coordinates stay in their original positions.

Keep PCB comparisons at their original SVG sizes and let the renderer fit all geometry, including annotations outside the board. Both boards now appear completely, with the original unit labels and scale bars. The existing snapshot filenames are retained; LM5155 and LMG342 require no visual snapshot changes.

![After: complete DRV8307 source and generated boards with units](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/00d2b4d7c2a5e747ba9347f223139f0b52f2b6c2/tests/ti-evms/__snapshots__/ti-drv8307evm-roundtrip-pcb-comparison.snap.svg)

body:
## Motivation

PCB vias should survive Circuit JSON → tscircuit round trips. The TI EVM repros in #89 showed vias in the source board but omitted them from the generated board—for example, all 109 LM5155 vias disappeared.

## Before

The footprint converter handled pads and plated holes but had no handler for `pcb_via`. Those records never became JSX, so the generated board lost the via arrays visible around components.

![Before: LM5155 source and generated board with missing vias](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/47cdc0185b792a531c50bf7ea0e56a1532c2629f/tests/ti-evms/__snapshots__/ti-lm5155evm-fly-roundtrip-pcb-comparison.snap.svg)

## After

Register `convertVias` alongside the existing footprint converters. Each source via becomes a `<via>` with its position, hole and copper diameters, layer endpoints, and tenting.

Support the legacy `is_tented` field emitted by [altium-to-circuit-json at the fixture generation commit](https://github.com/tscircuit/altium-to-circuit-json/blob/9a578b5762e1dcca06e6d3f84f1d2950d0acc301/lib/pcb/routing/convertPcbVia.ts), with explicit per-side tenting taking precedence. Reject vias without resolvable layer endpoints with an error naming the via.

The four TI EVM round trips now preserve all source vias: LM5155 (109), LM251772 (261), DRV8307 (360), and LMG342 (411). PCB and inline TSX snapshots are refreshed; schematic snapshots are unchanged.

![After: LM5155 source and generated board with restored vias](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/ff357d2a02004c418bc45f767155ac19bcf64bc9/tests/ti-evms/__snapshots__/ti-lm5155evm-fly-roundtrip-pcb-comparison.snap.svg)

## Validation

- Regression tests verify through, blind, and buried via geometry, layers, tenting, and missing-layer rejection.
- All four TI EVM tests compare rendered via counts against the source counts; all four PCB comparisons were visually checked.
- Additional runtime checks verify reversed layer endpoints and all supported tenting modes, including modern flags overriding legacy tenting.
- GitHub CI passes Bun tests, Type Check, and Format Check on `ff357d2`.
- The local snapshot-summary anomaly also occurs on the unchanged base, which exits successfully; all affected snapshots pass.
- Vercel preview requires maintainer authorization.

title: Use board-aware through-hole layers in the converter runtime
description: Updates the converter runtime to use board-aware through-hole layers, aligning Circuit JSON with its 0.0.507 schema and retaining Zod 3 peer, while adding regression tests for various layer configurations.
body:
Through-hole ports on a converted two-layer board include nonexistent inner layers with the old test/site runtime. Update `tscircuit` to 0.0.2696, align Circuit JSON with its 0.0.507 schema, and explicitly retain its Zod 3 peer. The underlying board-aware plated-hole layer fix already exists in tscircuit/core#2690.

Adds an actual Circuit JSON -> TSX -> runtime regression for 2-, 4-, 6-, and 10-layer boards. Refreshes the four TI EVM schematic snapshots affected by the newer runtime; PCB snapshots remain unchanged. Found during #89.

Validation: 29 converter/CLI tests pass, all four TI EVM round trips pass, and the package build passes. The existing test20 expected-failure repro is unchanged.

title: Preserve componentName when converting a board
description: Preserves the requested componentName when converting a board, allowing for named exports alongside default exports, and adds regression tests to ensure correct functionality.
body:
Board inputs currently ignore the requested `componentName` and emit an anonymous default export. Pass the option to the board template and emit a named component plus its default export. Direct `getBoardUsingTemplate` callers that omit the name keep the existing anonymous output.

Adds a runtime regression proving that the generated named/default exports render exactly one board, and updates the empty-board and four TI EVM inline snapshots. Found during the audit of #89.

Validation: 29 converter/CLI tests pass and the package build passes. The four TI EVM tests also passed during the full-suite run. The repository's existing `test20` remains an expected-failure repro; its stale snapshot was left unchanged.

title: Preserve source port pin attributes in generated chip TSX
description: Circuit JSON can contain a pins electrical requirements, but converting it to a chip currently drops them. This loses information such as the F1C100S AVCC pin requiring 2.8 V and the AP2127K-2.8TRG1 output providing 2.8 V. Generate the chips pinAttributes directly from source_port records. Map electrical fields to the tscircuitprops names and convert supportedconfigured capability flags into capabilitiesactiveCapabilities. Preserve explicit false and zero values, use physical pin numbers when available and names otherwise, omit empty attributes, and keep caller overrides working. Avoid combining multiple components attributes into one chip. No dependencies or lockfile changes. Validation: Five new regression tests cover all 89 F1C100S pins and five regulator pins, directionoutput modes, pull resistors, capabilities, numericstring voltages and capacitances, missing attributes, named pins, component isolation, and caller overrides. Live parts-engine  enriched Circuit JSON  converter  TSX verification preserves every attribute from both production datasheets (capability arrays compared as sets). Generated attributes validate against the current tscircuitprops schema, including the correct 2.8 V requirement and output. Full suite: 37 tests pass, zero failures (the existing test.failing for dropped board children accounts for the expected failed snapshot). Typecheck, build, and formatting pass. Pairs with https:github.comtscircuitparts-enginepull60 and the merged Circuit JSON schema extension https:github.comtscircuitcircuit-jsonpull850. This moves TSX generation into the converter; downstream CLI integration should consume enriched Circuit JSON instead of rewriting generated source as in https:github.comtscircuitclipull5063.
body:
Circuit JSON can contain a pin's electrical requirements, but converting it to a chip currently drops them. This loses information such as the F1C100S AVCC pin requiring 2.8 V and the AP2127K-2.8TRG1 output providing 2.8 V.

Generate the chip's `pinAttributes` directly from `source_port` records. Map electrical fields to the `@tscircuit/props` names and convert supported/configured capability flags into `capabilities`/`activeCapabilities`. Preserve explicit false and zero values, use physical pin numbers when available and names otherwise, omit empty attributes, and keep caller overrides working. Avoid combining multiple components' attributes into one chip. No dependencies or lockfile changes.

Validation:
- Five new regression tests cover all 89 F1C100S pins and five regulator pins, direction/output modes, pull resistors, capabilities, numeric/string voltages and capacitances, missing attributes, named pins, component isolation, and caller overrides.
- Live parts-engine → enriched Circuit JSON → converter → TSX verification preserves every attribute from both production datasheets (capability arrays compared as sets). Generated attributes validate against the current `@tscircuit/props` schema, including the correct 2.8 V requirement and output.
- Full suite: 37 tests pass, zero failures (the existing `test.failing` for dropped board children accounts for the expected failed snapshot). Typecheck, build, and formatting pass.

Pairs with https://github.com/tscircuit/parts-engine/pull/60 and the merged Circuit JSON schema extension https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/850. This moves TSX generation into the converter; downstream CLI integration should consume enriched Circuit JSON instead of rewriting generated source as in https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5063.

body:
Higher effort previously changed routing/search heuristics, and extra early simplification could leave worse routes for DRC repair. Cap routing, force-improvement, and repair tuning at 1x while preserving lower-effort behavior. Pipeline 9 now spends extra effort after DRC repair: 1.5x evaluates one additional cleanup pass and 2x evaluates two. It retains a candidate only if it passes DRC and reduces vias, or keeps the same via count with fewer route points. Length matching and power-trace expansion run afterward. Cleanup and outer iteration budgets allow the additional work.

Add `/benchmark-effort` to compare pipeline 9 on all of dataset18 at 1x, 1.5x, and 2x on one Blacksmith runner. Per-sample timeouts scale to 600s/900s/1200s. The report shows completion, DRC, timeouts, matched runtime, and per-sample/aggregate vias; JSON reports are retained as artifacts. Fix the existing benchmark CLI truncating `--effort 1.5` to 1, and verify the effective effort in every comparison report.

Validation: all nine CI test shards, build, type check, format check, and added-code check passed; local build and type checking also passed; focused tests cover effective fractional effort, unchanged initial routing, baseline cleanup budgets, input immutability, and rejection of invalid optimization candidates. Higher-effort snapshot updates retain their DRC assertions and use separate Linux/macOS expectations where routes differ. Full dataset18 comparison completed successfully. All 16 samples solved and passed relaxed DRC at every effort, with zero timeouts and no per-sample via-count increases.

The PR-comment command becomes available when the dispatcher/parser changes reach the default branch. Pre-merge comparison can be dispatched through the existing Autorouting Benchmark workflow on this branch with `effort_compare=true`, the full commit SHA, and this PR number.


Dataset18 results on one Blacksmith runner:

| Effort | Solved / relaxed DRC passing | Total vias | Change vs 1x | Sum of sample runtimes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1x | 16/16 | 3,576 | — | 2,227.7s |
| 1.5x | 16/16 | 3,555 | -21 | 2,324.6s |
| 2x | 16/16 | 3,554 | -22 | 2,401.6s |

The improvement is modest but monotonic: 1.5x removes 21 vias, and 2x removes one additional via. No individual sample gains vias. The previously regressing sample 15 remains DRC-clean with 349 vias at all three efforts.

[Benchmark run and JSON artifacts](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36793259438). The run uses solver revision `fd9f0e4b6`; subsequent commits only update labels, formatting, snapshots, and test expectations.

title: Pin Repair03 to upstream via-index squash commit
description: Replace the Repair03 fork integration pin with the exact upstream squash commit from high-density-repair03 144.
body:
## Summary

Replace the Repair03 fork integration pin with the exact upstream squash commit from [high-density-repair03 #144](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/144).

- Previous: `Abse2001/high-density-repair03@ac744fcc8cc4e83fbf12769507e963c974f5932f`.
- Proposed: `tscircuit/high-density-repair03@ccad3906eb0fe30c9f79f4e28f390d9f41cbf387`.
- Based on autorouter main `38a1ee35516cee0a7b1fa9ce80f6c94bb4ab985f` (0.0.948), which already includes merged through-via fix [#2740](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740) and its distant-pad lookup optimization.

The production change is one dependency line in `package.json`. Three Linux SVG snapshots are refreshed from actual CI output after native before/after image review. No routing code, test source, assertions, input, DRC policy or timeouts are changed. The repository disables lockfile saving. Performance optimization is explicitly deferred to a separate PR.

## Important validation caveat

This is a draft validation PR, not a claim that the new hash is equivalent to the previous integration.

Repair03 #144 was squash-merged into `fix/broad-repulsion-trace-pad-width`, not Repair03 main. Its parent is the squash commit of [#143](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/143), `5698b2d623c1af9194415a6c55cb8d7e3a86c015`, so both upstream via fixes are included.

However, the branch differs from the autorouter's current fork integration. Inspection shows that the proposed dependency lacks immutable-geometry/static-connectivity DRC caches, non-plated-hole clearance handling, and some safe-layer search/nearby-via safeguards present in `ac744fcc`. It also contains different portfolio incumbent retention and via-pad repulsion logic. These are dependency-tree differences, not extra edits in this PR. Consequently, earlier benchmark results cannot establish that this pin is safe; completion, DRC and timing must be measured again. Do not merge solely because it references a merged PR.

## Validation

- `bun install` succeeds with the exact upstream archive. The installed Repair03 DRC-engine source matches `ccad3906` byte-for-byte.
- Four focused tests pass locally, 53 assertions: fixed via drill spans, inner-layer via transition identity, shared-site via identity, and geometry-first connected-pad filtering. No local full-board routing or benchmarks.
- **All ordinary CI is green on snapshot-only commit `530f4aa7`**: [Bun Test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36778792678) passed all nine shards, and [build](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36778792816), [typecheck](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36778792797), [format](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36778792561), [added-code check](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36778792629), [GitHub Vercel Build](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36778792683), and [external Vercel](https://vercel.com/tscircuit/capacity-node-autorouter/EkVaHCgXXwPk3BMqDeAwvFF61J18) all passed. The prior [Bun Test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36772140844) failed only three snapshot comparisons: `bugreport96-full-gameboy-no-breakout` (1.386%, threshold 1%), `bugreport94-56fa2e` (35.944%), and `bugreport88-9a86ed` (27.023%). Their preceding routing assertions passed; #94 and #88 also passed connection-set and explicit zero-reference-DRC assertions. #96 is the older preloaded Game Boy fixture, not the full-board platform input below. The three expected snapshots were copied byte-for-byte from native Linux `.received.svg` files after before/after PNG review. No tolerances or assertions changed, and no benchmarks were repeated for this snapshot-only commit.
- Snapshot provenance: nodes 6 and 8 of run `36772140844`; SHA256 hashes are `6e9f26a28c40ce27428a9946fd3b7914d73ba497e6610848bd33f122c915d476` (#88), `7d1b3af454a05771f4924999973278cfecf615d33e890a39e66f590fc3dd61ae` (#94), and `568090418469e5b7abf06f79e2bca709d273fa692864e9ae568873f681a47aef` (#96). Source and destination bytes match for all three. No local full-board rerouting was performed.
- Pipeline 9 same-machine benchmarks were requested through [this PR comment](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2794#issuecomment-5919029027): `/benchmark-all --pipeline 9 --same-machine`. Both compare main `38a1ee3` and PR `9f72275`.
- [Dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2794#issuecomment-5919044953) is complete: **85/85 complete and relaxed-DRC-passing (100%) on both, 0 issues, 0 timeouts, 0 outcome changes**. Raw reports also confirm no per-sample via or odd-angle-warning changes. Average vias 38.99 on both. Timing percentiles in seconds, main → PR: P50 2.989→3.121, P60 4.743→4.522, P70 5.756→5.651, P80 8.337→7.825, P90 10.203→10.353, P95 12.689→11.771. These are mixed timing changes, not a uniform speedup.
- [SRJ18 final report](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2794#issuecomment-5919045927): **completion and relaxed-DRC pass regress from 16/16 (100%) to 15/16 (93.75%)**. Timeouts increase **0→1**. **Sample14 is the only outcome regression**, from main completing DRC-free in **352.837 seconds** to PR timing out at the unchanged **360-second** limit. The last observed stage is `pipeline9JointDrcRepairSolver` / `Pipeline9JointDrcRepairSolver`, phase iteration 28, pipeline progress 88%. This is an actual completion regression, not merely a slower passing sample. No improved outcome samples.
- All 15 completed SRJ18 samples remain relaxed-DRC-passing; total reported issues are **0→0 among completed samples**, not a zero-DRC result for timed-out sample14. Sample15 completes with 0 DRCs on both but is slower: **313.395→340.520 seconds**. Its joint-repair time rises 69.730→81.640 seconds; all timing changes still need causal profiling before attributing them to a particular removed optimization.
- SRJ18 timing percentiles in seconds, main → PR: P50 **103.383→105.133**, P60 **135.980→148.621**, P70 **177.659→188.860**, P80 **268.247→276.577**, P90 **295.396→315.172**, P95 **323.256→345.390**. Timeout samples count at their configured timeout in these percentiles.
- The report's average vias **223.50→219.67** is **not an improvement**: the PR average excludes timed-out sample14's 281 baseline vias. On the same 15 completed samples, both average **219.67**, with every per-sample via count unchanged. Average odd-angle warnings **575.19→564.93** is likewise affected by that exclusion. The only real per-sample style change is sample6 **1162→1159** odd-angle warnings; the other completed samples are unchanged. On matched completed samples the odd-angle average is **565.13→564.93**.
- [Full Game Boy Linux/macOS validation](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36772171046) **passed** at `9f72275a40f477b6465160518537b8b6a608361f`: **322 traces, 288 vias, 0 reference relaxed DRCs**. Downloaded `routes.json`, `summary.json`, `drc-errors.json` and `board.svg` are byte-identical between OSs and to the previously verified output. Input hash remains `89cfabf40f44453f4894a67475c4a5563e171d629f52bd42a8724bb15185ace4`; route hash remains `e6bdeafeeed9b4603a207c7aa443f232b1945d997c29fb318a720a55de7722f8`. This is direct artifact comparison, not an inference from the workflow's summary-only comparison. Identical copper preserves the prior zero through-via-contact result. No Game Boy project or validation-only PR #2741 changes.

### Requested SRJ18-only rerun

[Rerun report](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2794#issuecomment-5919499748), [run 36775408401](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36775408401), compares the same `38a1ee3` and `9f72275` revisions. Both complete and pass relaxed DRC on **14/16 samples (87.5%)**, with **0 issues among completed samples and 2 timeouts**. Samples **14 and 15** time out at 360 seconds in joint DRC repair on both sides: zero changed outcomes in this run. Average vias are 210.43 on both; P50 time is 124.6→119.7 seconds and P95 is 360 seconds on both.

This does not erase the earlier PR-only sample14 timeout. The first run used Blacksmith host generation 2 (Ampere); the rerun used generation 1 (ARM). The logged Bun version, effort and 88 installed package entries per side were unchanged between runs. Every completed main sample ran 9–31% slower on the rerun with unchanged high-density/pathing iteration counts. Same-machine pairing applies within each run, not across separate workflow runs. No timeouts were raised or routing code changed to obtain either result. Optimization and timeout-headroom work is deferred to a separate PR at the user's request; no additional benchmark is needed for the snapshot-only update.

The unchanged Game Boy copper does not establish fabrication readiness: the previous separate Repair03 analysis found five clearance findings, and the minimum emitted wire width remains near 0.01667 mm. A zero benchmark DRC count is not full manufacturing approval. The dependency-coverage differences above also remain relevant even if a benchmark passes.

No automatic merge requested.

## Final assessment

**CI maintenance is separate from regression clearance.** All ordinary CI is now verified green at `530f4aa7` after the three reviewed snapshot updates. Dataset01 and the current full Game Boy output are unchanged. SRJ18 had one new timeout in the first run and two shared timeouts in the rerun, so a blanket no-regression claim is not established. The dependency-coverage differences remain documented above. At the user's request this PR receives only the snapshot/CI maintenance; optimization belongs in a separate PR. Nothing is merged automatically, and green CI must not be interpreted as resolving the timeout or fabrication caveats.
