title: Fix through-via drill spans in Pipeline 9 routing and repair
description: Summary Fix through-via handling in Pipeline 9 and its Repair03 dependency. This PR targets main directly and contains the fix, focused regression tests, related existing-testsnapshot updates, and CI timeout classification for the existing SRJ18 sample 2 tests. It does not add the full Game Boy repro, its input, or its snapshot. The Game Boy stays in validation-only repro 2741(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2741), not for merging. No merge or auto-merge has been requested.  Bug When allowBlindAndBuriedVias is false or omitted, a via connecting top to inner1 still occupies every copper layer. Its signal transition does not define its drill span. Using only the signal layers lets a foreign net pass through the via on inner2 or bottom.  Fix Pipeline 9 fixed-copper geometry, nodeB01 obstacle selection, and regional collision checks use the existing board via policy. Through vias reserve all board layers; explicitly allowed blindburied vias retain their limited span. The geometry cache includes layer count and via policy. Repair03 is pinned to ac744fcc(https:github.comAbse2001high-density-repair03commitac744fcc8cc4e83fbf12769507e963c974f5932f): an integration commit on top of the existing cbbc86a3 pin, porting merged 143(https:github.comtscircuithigh-density-repair03pull143) drill-span handling and still-open 144(https:github.comtscircuithigh-density-repair03pull144), which refreshes via point indexes after a trace detour. Existing optimizations and invalid-endpoint checks are preserved. This is a fork integration pin, not an upstream release or the exact head of 144. Current main already includes the clearance-margin transition-identity correction and the newer trace-simplification via-preservation fix from 2779(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2779). The merge retains both; the transition-identity production code is no longer an additional diff in this PR. Signal endpoints and component-owned through-obstacle geometry are unchanged. No board-specific routing cases, new feature flags, or suppressed invariant failures.  Dependency and merge order Review and merge Repair03 144 first, then replace the integration pin with an upstream commit containing both fixes and the existing pinned behavior before merging this autorouter PR. Revalidate after changing the pin; do not assume another branch or package version is equivalent. 143 is merged; 144 was still open when checked on September 30. No PR will be merged automatically.  Focused regression tests pipeline9-fixed-via-drill-span: falsedefaulttrue via policy, every copper layer, collisions in both argument orders, layer-countcache changes, and invalid transitions. pipeline9-b01-through-via-obstacle: an actual bottom-layer route avoids a top-to-inner1 through via; explicitly permitting blind vias makes bottom available. Completion, clearance, and endpoints are checked. Its one native snapshot shows captured B01 solver states before and after routing, following Seves snapshot guidance(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2193pullrequestreview-4998204680). pipeline9-clearance-margin-through-via-transition: an inner-layer signal transition remains valid inside a through via without losing transition identity. After merging main and installing the actual merged dependencies, these three tests plus mains pipeline9-clearance-margin-tracks-via-identity passed locally: 4 tests, 73 assertions. No full-board routing or dataset benchmarks were run locally.  Timeout investigation and optimization  September 30 Latest head 13dc4a0f adds only an early geometry rejection in getConnectedPadSides plus one focused regression test. It skips net-connectivity lookups for pads that cannot contain the route terminal. The same layer test, 0.001 mm tolerance, connected-net predicate, output ordering, routing rules and dependency pins remain unchanged. The new test failed before the optimization (4 unnecessary lookups) and passes afterward. Three focused tests pass with 36 assertions. The previous standard SRJ18 benchmark(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2740issuecomment-5915973380) at 5680cbdc did regress completion from 1616 to 1416: samples 14 and 15 timed out at 360 seconds in joint repair. Dataset01 stayed 8585 complete and DRC-passing. The new benchmark below follows an actual optimization, not an unchanged retry; the earlier failures and sample14s limited timeout margin remain relevant. GitHub CPU profiling(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36756273653) compared exact main e85fb193 and PR 5680cbdc with identical sample inputs. All four serial diagnostic solves completed with zero relaxed DRCs, but this is a different runnerworkload from the normal eight-worker benchmark, not proof that its timeout regression is resolved. Sample14 joint-repair wall time rose from 75.52 to 107.39 seconds. CPU samples locate most additional work in bounded regional clearance search (54.97 to 71.39 sampled seconds) and regional B01 repair (7.83 to 22.02). Repair03 portfolio time was only about 7.35 to 7.70 seconds; its via-index refresh was not the dominant measured cost. Sample15 serial total time was approximately unchanged (197.49 to 196.87 seconds). Its profile nevertheless identified about 6.01 sampled seconds of net lookup work beneath the pad-side helper, motivating the geometry-first change. This does not remove sample14s larger clearance-search cost. The completed beforeafter optimization profile(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns36760525317) compares old PR 5680cbdc (directory label main, not repository main) against 13dc4a0f. Both samples have byte-identical input, route JSON and DRC JSON before and after, unchanged routing iterations and clearance-search work counts, and zero relaxed DRCs. Sample14 remains 238 traces281 vias; sample15 remains 461 traces349 vias. Diagnostic instrumentation stays outside this PR. Sample14 pad-helper inclusive sampled CPU time fell 1.892 to 0.061 seconds, but serial total time was 249.972 to 254.176 seconds (1.7). Sample15 helper CPU fell 8.917 to 0.060 seconds, with serial total time 201.698 to 190.490 seconds (-5.6). This confirms the unnecessary lookup cost was removed without changing copper; it does not show a uniform end-to-end speedup. These are profiler measurements on a serial runner, not the standard benchmark score.  Completed validation at 13dc4a0f Benchmark request by PR comment(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull2740issuecomment-5917460010): benchmark-all --pipeline 9 --same-machine. ## Summary

Fix through-via handling in Pipeline 9 and its Repair03 dependency. This PR targets `main` directly and contains the fix, focused regression tests, related existing-test/snapshot updates, and CI timeout classification for the existing SRJ18 sample 2 tests. It does not add the full Game Boy repro, its input, or its snapshot.

The Game Boy stays in [validation-only repro #2741](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2741), not for merging. No merge or auto-merge has been requested.

## Bug

When `allowBlindAndBuriedVias` is false or omitted, a via connecting top to inner1 still occupies every copper layer. Its signal transition does not define its drill span. Using only the signal layers lets a foreign net pass through the via on inner2 or bottom.

## Fix

- Pipeline 9 fixed-copper geometry, node/B01 obstacle selection, and regional collision checks use the existing board via policy. Through vias reserve all board layers; explicitly allowed blind/buried vias retain their limited span. The geometry cache includes layer count and via policy.
- Repair03 is pinned to [`ac744fcc`](https://github.com/Abse2001/high-density-repair03/commit/ac744fcc8cc4e83fbf12769507e963c974f5932f): an integration commit on top of the existing `cbbc86a3` pin, porting merged [#143](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/143) drill-span handling and still-open [#144](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/144), which refreshes via point indexes after a trace detour. Existing optimizations and invalid-endpoint checks are preserved. This is a fork integration pin, not an upstream release or the exact head of #144.
- Current main already includes the clearance-margin transition-identity correction and the newer trace-simplification via-preservation fix from [#2779](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2779). The merge retains both; the transition-identity production code is no longer an additional diff in this PR.

Signal endpoints and component-owned through-obstacle geometry are unchanged. No board-specific routing cases, new feature flags, or suppressed invariant failures.

### Dependency and merge order

Review and merge Repair03 #144 first, then replace the integration pin with an upstream commit containing both fixes and the existing pinned behavior before merging this autorouter PR. Revalidate after changing the pin; do not assume another branch or package version is equivalent. #143 is merged; #144 was still open when checked on September 30. No PR will be merged automatically.

## Focused regression tests

- `pipeline9-fixed-via-drill-span`: false/default/true via policy, every copper layer, collisions in both argument orders, layer-count/cache changes, and invalid transitions.
- `pipeline9-b01-through-via-obstacle`: an actual bottom-layer route avoids a top-to-inner1 through via; explicitly permitting blind vias makes bottom available. Completion, clearance, and endpoints are checked. Its one native snapshot shows captured B01 solver states before and after routing, following [Seve's snapshot guidance](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2193#pullrequestreview-4998204680).
- `pipeline9-clearance-margin-through-via-transition`: an inner-layer signal transition remains valid inside a through via without losing transition identity.

After merging main and installing the actual merged dependencies, these three tests plus main's `pipeline9-clearance-margin-tracks-via-identity` passed locally: **4 tests, 73 assertions**. No full-board routing or dataset benchmarks were run locally.

## Timeout investigation and optimization — September 30

**Latest head `13dc4a0f` adds only an early geometry rejection in `getConnectedPadSides` plus one focused regression test.** It skips net-connectivity lookups for pads that cannot contain the route terminal. The same layer test, 0.001 mm tolerance, connected-net predicate, output ordering, routing rules and dependency pins remain unchanged. The new test failed before the optimization (4 unnecessary lookups) and passes afterward. Three focused tests pass with 36 assertions.

The [previous standard SRJ18 benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5915973380) at `5680cbdc` **did regress completion from 16/16 to 14/16**: samples 14 and 15 timed out at 360 seconds in joint repair. Dataset01 stayed 85/85 complete and DRC-passing. The new benchmark below follows an actual optimization, not an unchanged retry; the earlier failures and sample14's limited timeout margin remain relevant.

[GitHub CPU profiling](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36756273653) compared exact main `e85fb193` and PR `5680cbdc` with identical sample inputs. All four serial diagnostic solves completed with zero relaxed DRCs, but **this is a different runner/workload from the normal eight-worker benchmark**, not proof that its timeout regression is resolved.

- Sample14 joint-repair wall time rose from 75.52 to 107.39 seconds. CPU samples locate most additional work in bounded regional clearance search (54.97 to 71.39 sampled seconds) and regional B01 repair (7.83 to 22.02). Repair03 portfolio time was only about 7.35 to 7.70 seconds; its via-index refresh was not the dominant measured cost.
- Sample15 serial total time was approximately unchanged (197.49 to 196.87 seconds). Its profile nevertheless identified about 6.01 sampled seconds of net lookup work beneath the pad-side helper, motivating the geometry-first change. This does not remove sample14's larger clearance-search cost.
- The completed [before/after optimization profile](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36760525317) compares old PR `5680cbdc` (directory label `main`, not repository main) against `13dc4a0f`. Both samples have **byte-identical input, route JSON and DRC JSON** before and after, unchanged routing iterations and clearance-search work counts, and zero relaxed DRCs. Sample14 remains 238 traces/281 vias; sample15 remains 461 traces/349 vias. Diagnostic instrumentation stays outside this PR.
- Sample14 pad-helper inclusive sampled CPU time fell **1.892 to 0.061 seconds**, but serial total time was **249.972 to 254.176 seconds** (+1.7%). Sample15 helper CPU fell **8.917 to 0.060 seconds**, with serial total time **201.698 to 190.490 seconds** (-5.6%). This confirms the unnecessary lookup cost was removed without changing copper; it does not show a uniform end-to-end speedup. These are profiler measurements on a serial runner, not the standard benchmark score.

### Completed validation at `13dc4a0f`

- [Benchmark request by PR comment](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5917460010): `/benchmark-all --pipeline 9 --same-machine`. Both completed reports compare main `e85fb193` with PR `13dc4a0f`.

| [Dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5917472134) (85 scenarios) | 85/85 → 85/85 (100%) | 85/85 → 85/85 (100%) | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 38.99 → 38.99 |
| [SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5917472637) (16 scenarios) | 16/16 → 16/16 (100%) | 16/16 → 16/16 (100%) | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 224.00 → 223.50 |

**No improved or regressed completion/DRC/timeout outcomes among these 101 samples.** In this new run, both previously timed-out samples complete with zero relaxed DRCs: sample14 **332.931 → 350.864 seconds**, sample15 **328.781 → 306.854 seconds** (main → PR). Sample14 has only **9.136 seconds of headroom** below the unchanged 360-second timeout. The tested head meets the no-outcome-regression requirement in this run, but is not a guarantee against future runtime variation or proof that its larger regional-search cost is solved.

Timing percentiles in seconds (main → PR), kept separate from routing outcomes:

| Dataset | P50 | P60 | P70 | P80 | P90 | P95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dataset01 | 3.48 → 3.36 | 5.07 → 5.20 | 6.15 → 6.21 | 8.85 → 8.81 | 11.27 → 11.92 | 12.82 → 13.41 |
| SRJ18 | 104.40 → 106.48 | 132.42 → 142.86 | 200.33 → 187.79 | 242.64 → 262.60 | 310.64 → 295.20 | 329.82 → 317.86 |

SRJ18 aggregate joint-repair time is 421.715 → 470.144 seconds. Timing is mixed, not a uniform improvement.

Every SRJ18 via-count change: sample6 **278→281**, sample8 **283→284**, sample12 **304→302**, sample13 **213→196**, sample14 **277→281**, sample15 **344→349**, sample16 **111→109**. All other via counts, including every Dataset01 sample, are unchanged.

Every odd-angle warning change (style, not DRC failures):

- SRJ18 decreases: sample2 **1547→925**, sample7 **312→123**, sample11 **524→519**, sample12 **900→897**, sample13 **594→575**, sample15 **1056→1012**, sample16 **377→364**.
- SRJ18 increases: sample3 **150→275**, sample6 **1049→1162**, sample8 **986→1026**, sample9 **268→269**, sample14 **712→726**. Average **612.81→575.19**.
- Dataset01: only sample71 changes, **76→75**; average **7.45→7.44**.

- [Game Boy Linux/macOS revalidation](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36760357113) passed on `13dc4a0f`: **322 traces, 288 vias, 0 reference relaxed DRCs**. Downloaded `routes.json`, `summary.json`, `drc-errors.json` and `board.svg` are byte-identical between both OSs and to the previous verified output. Route SHA256 remains `e6bdeafeeed9b4603a207c7aa443f232b1945d997c29fb318a720a55de7722f8`; input SHA256 remains `89cfabf40f44453f4894a67475c4a5563e171d629f52bd42a8724bb15185ace4`. The identical copper preserves the prior zero through-via-contact result and the separate clearance/width caveats below. PR #2741 and the Game Boy project were not changed.
- **All applicable ordinary CI is green at `13dc4a0f`:** [all nine Bun Test shards](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36760305003), build, typecheck, format, code-hack check, Testbox, GitHub Vercel Build and external Vercel passed. No snapshot or assertion changes were needed for this optimization.

No timeouts, DRC rules, assertions, snapshots, or through-via protection were weakened. No sample-specific cases or new flags were introduced. The Game Boy's earlier zero *reference relaxed* DRC result is not fabrication approval; the separate checker/trace-width caveats below remain.

## Previous validation — main 0.0.946

Main advanced while the previous snapshot update was being verified: [#2776](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2776) changes clearance repair and reduces board-1726's Linux baseline to 59 DRCs. Production head `3a86612e` merges main `d3507489` (0.0.946), retaining that improvement and **main's unchanged `<=59` assertion**. The old PR-only `<=88` assertion and explanation are removed.

The new conflict was limited to the board-1726 test and its Linux snapshot, initially resolved using main's versions. Repair03 remains `ac744fcc`; all other dependency pins match main. The three other Linux snapshot refreshes from the previous run passed in the latest CI.

Six focused tests, including both new upstream independent-bend repair regressions, pass locally with **87 assertions**. [CI run 36695044821](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36695044821) passed eight of nine test shards and all non-test checks (build, typecheck, format, check-added-code, Blacksmith Testbox, GitHub Vercel Build, and external Vercel). The sole failure was board-1726's Linux snapshot mismatch; all its routing, repair-improvement, and `<=59` assertions passed.

**Board-1726 improves from main's 59 DRCs to 55 (-4).** Commit `527b1fff` updates only its expected Linux snapshot using the unchanged `.received.svg` from job `109820898491`, after reviewing the native before/after PNG. SHA256: `6df102208969152036a5a606a529713a007cafd4f050fa2c925057af6944ee29`. No code, test assertions, tolerances, timeouts, inputs, or dependencies changed. **CI on this snapshot-only head is now green:** [all nine Bun Test shards passed](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36696968271), as did build, typecheck, format, check-added-code, Blacksmith Testbox, GitHub Vercel Build, and external Vercel. Board-1726 passed its native snapshot and unchanged numeric assertions.

Fresh same-machine benchmarks were requested by [PR comment](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5908100015), comparing main `d3507489` with production head `3a86612e`:

- [Dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5908112979): 85/85 complete and DRC-passing on both, 0 issues, 0 timeouts, 0 outcome changes, 38.99 average vias on both. P50 2.9 to 3.0s (+2.4%); P95 11.8 to 12.1s (+2.8%).
- [SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5908114645): 16/16 complete and DRC-passing on both, 0 issues, 0 timeouts, 0 improved/regressed outcomes. Average vias 224.00 to 223.50; angled-trace warnings 612.81 to 575.19. P50 103.2 to 107.3s (+3.9%), P80 237.4 to 267.5s (+12.7%), P95 314.6 to 331.8s (+5.5%). Joint-repair aggregate time 396.664 to 458.258s. This run has slower timing but no newly failing, DRC-failing, or timed-out samples, including sample 14.

Raw SRJ18 reports confirm the following via-count changes (all remain routed and DRC-passing): sample6 278→281, sample8 283→284, sample12 304→302, sample13 213→196, sample14 277→281, sample15 344→349, sample16 111→109. No other sample's via count changed. Sample14 completed in 334.65s→354.03s, close to its 360s timeout; sample15 completed in 307.93s→324.40s. Treat that reduced timing margin as a risk, not an observed timeout.

Odd-angle warning changes are mixed: improved samples2 (1547→925),7 (312→123),11 (524→519),12 (900→897),13 (594→575),15 (1056→1012),16 (377→364); increased samples3 (150→275),6 (1049→1162),8 (986→1026),9 (268→269),14 (712→726). These are style warnings, not new DRC/completion failures.

This comparison was rerun because main's production routing code changed. Snapshot-only commit `527b1fff` does not require another benchmark. The older results below are historical, not proof for this implementation.

## Previous validation — main 0.0.945

Head [`25a63051`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/commit/25a63051d9537cb9eb7ec82f46cf9746fc80d268) merges main [`a047b995`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/commit/a047b99546e956935de269d5e9c8123b029ffd55), version 0.0.945. GitHub reports the conflicts resolved. The Repair03 pin is unchanged; main's newer simplifier pin `63589c4` is retained.

Six conflicts were in generated SVG snapshots only. Those were resolved using main's native baselines, not hand-edited drawings. Actual Linux CI output will determine which need refreshing. Assertions, input, tolerances, and solver budgets were not changed during this merge.

- On merge head `25a63051`, build, typecheck, format, check-added-code, Blacksmith Testbox, GitHub Vercel Build, and external Vercel passed. [Bun Test](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36693144058) passed five shards and failed four solely on snapshot mismatches; there were no numeric assertion, install, or timeout failures.
- Follow-up `1a35f237` refreshed only those four snapshots from that run's actual Linux `.received.svg` files, reviewed as before/after PNGs and SHA256-verified byte-for-byte. No solver code, dependencies, tests, assertions, tolerances, or timeouts changed in that commit. It was superseded by the new main merge described above.
- The four snapshots are board-1726 (node1), same-net-via-clearance-repair-visual (node2), default-via-is-through-hole-visual (node7), and T113 HDMI board-and-drills (node4). Same-net visual input changes 91 to 86 errors while output stays 70; default-via visual stays at 4; T113's routing and drill-spacing assertions pass.
- **On the 0.0.945 baseline, board-1726 regressed from main's 80 DRCs to PR's 87 (+7).** Its then-existing `<=88` and repair-improvement assertions passed without modification. Updating that snapshot recorded the regression; it did not establish no-regression or fabrication readiness. Current main now uses the stricter 59-DRC baseline, pending fresh results.
- The [new benchmark comment](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5907806163) requests `/benchmark-all --pipeline 9 --same-machine`. The current dispatcher runs Dataset01 and SRJ18; both compare main `a047b995` against production head `25a63051`. Snapshot-only updates do not change the benchmarked implementation.
- [New Dataset01 report](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5907818077): **85/85 complete and DRC-passing on both**, 0 issues, 0 timeouts, 0 improved/regressed outcomes, 38.99 average vias on both. P50 2.8 to 2.9s (+4.2%); P95 12.3 to 11.3s (-8.2%).
- [SRJ18 report for 0.0.945](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5907819177): **16/16 complete and DRC-passing on both**, 0 issues, 0 timeouts, 0 improved/regressed outcomes. Average vias 224.00 to 223.50. P50 104.7 to 105.6s (+0.8%); P95 325.3 to 322.8s (-0.8%). This completed comparison is encouraging, but does not validate the subsequent 0.0.946 merge.
- The separate Repair03-only [PR #2782](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2782) on this same main had a new SRJ18 sample 14 timeout (16/16 to 15/16 completed). That is not proof of this combined fix's result, but is a regression to watch in the new comparison.

## Historical results — not proof for the current merged head

On main 0.0.944 versus production candidate `f72dd50d`:

- [Dataset01 report](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5898175805): both 85/85 completed and DRC-passing, 0 DRC issues, 0 timeouts, 38.99 average vias.
- [SRJ18 report](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2740#issuecomment-5898176041): both 15/16 completed and DRC-passing, 0 issues among completed boards, the same sample 14 timeout. Average vias 221.00 to 220.07; sample 15 remained DRC-free but gained 7 vias.
- Board-1726 historically had an explicitly accepted 87 to 88 DRC change. That historical `<=88` assertion has since been removed in favor of current main's `<=59` check. Green assertions alone do not mean no regression.
- Sample 2 took 260.24s baseline to 300.24s candidate (+15.4%), mostly joint repair (54.29s to 92.66s). Both full-board sample 2 tests use the existing 600-second slow-test group. Other tests remain at 300 seconds and job budgets at 20 minutes. This is a CI allowance, not a runtime optimization. No further timeout changes were made in the main merge.
- All ordinary CI passed on previous head `9f914309`. The new head must pass independently.

Separate [historical Game Boy validation](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36626388346) had **109 relaxed DRCs and 9 through-via contacts**, versus baseline 108 / 12. Repair03 detected all remaining contacts but did not repair them all. Linux/Mac outputs were byte-identical. These older scores are superseded by the current validation below.

## Current Game Boy validation — separate PR #2741

At the author's request, validation-only [PR #2741](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2741) now tests this exact fix head `527b1fff` on the unchanged full board. [Workflow 36698662930](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36698662930), validation head `184d33cb`, completed on Linux and macOS with **322 traces, 288 vias, and 0 reference relaxed DRCs**. The downloaded route JSON, summary, DRC JSON and native board SVG are byte-identical between platforms. Routing took 176.90 s on Linux and 340.83 s on macOS.

Static analysis of the saved output reproduced zero reference errors and **zero actual through-via contacts outside signal layers**, with zero such contacts missed by Repair03. All 288 vias are converted as four-layer through vias. This is **109 → 0 reference findings and 9 → 0 through-via contacts** compared with the older combined implementation, but upstream clearance repair also changed, so this is not a same-main causal comparison of this PR alone.

Do not interpret this as fabrication ready: Repair03's separate indexed checker reports **5 clearance findings** (2 via-to-pad and 3 same-net via-spacing). The reference benchmark omits the via-to-pad pad-clearance check and uses drill-hole spacing where this Repair03 pin uses outer-copper spacing. Minimum emitted wire width remains about **0.01667 mm**. Details and artifact hashes are recorded in #2741. Those measurements preceded the current performance-only validation. The user subsequently authorized PR #2741 to assert zero reference relaxed DRCs and zero missed through-via contacts and use the actual native zero-DRC snapshot at head `a83ed089`. The current optimization does not modify that separate validation PR.

## Review conventions

Use precise drill-span terminology ([Seve's naming feedback](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/136#discussion_r4049612208)); keep Pipeline 9 semantics out of shared repair code ([review](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2577#pullrequestreview-5223366924)); preserve loud invariant failures and actual routed snapshots.

title: fix: preserve source board thickness in KiCad PCB exports
description: Fixes incorrect board thickness in KiCad PCB exports by preserving the source thickness instead of defaulting to 1.6 mm.
body:
KiCad PCB export currently writes 1.6 mm regardless of `pcb_board.thickness`. A board with 0.8, 1.2, or 2.0 mm thickness therefore exports with the wrong physical dimension. This change preserves the source thickness in millimeters and keeps the existing 1.6 mm fallback when thickness or the board is absent.

The regression test generates CircuitJSON with tscircuit and parses the exported KiCad PCB. It covers non-default values, explicit 1.6 mm, the generated 1.4 mm default, omitted thickness, a missing board, unit-string normalization, and zero/negative numeric values accepted by the existing schema. No new validation is introduced. The existing rotated-pad text fixture now expects its source's 1.4 mm thickness; the USB-C model fixture explicitly requests the 1.6 mm thickness depicted by its existing 3D snapshot.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.3.14 and native KiCad 10.0.6, against upstream v0.0.225 (`b2ae976ac56e2e7ded637c4af17327c6f30ca300`):

- Before the fix, the new regression fails: expected 0.8 mm, received 1.6 mm.
- After the fix, the three affected tests pass: 43 assertions and one snapshot.
- Native KiCad reads the exported 0.8, 1.2, and 2.0 mm values, the generated default, and the omitted-thickness fallback correctly.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, `bun run format:check`, and lint on changed TypeScript files pass. Formatting has five existing oversized-fixture warnings; lint has two existing warnings. Formatting was run with generated debug output and downloaded third-party demos outside the checkout.
- Full `bun test`: 139 pass, 62 fail (201 tests). The same 62 failures also occur on unmodified upstream with the same installed dependencies and native KiCad on this Mac. Baseline: 136 pass, 64 fail (200 tests); two baseline environment/download failures pass with network/local-server access enabled. No new aggregate failures remain. The local aggregate suite is therefore not green, despite the targeted tests passing.

This PR contains only the exporter change, regression test, and two related fixture adjustments.

GitHub CI at `09ace9e8f88267881701707b066a909553179f7f`: all 201 tests pass in the repository's KiCad 10.0.1 container, including the new thickness regression and affected fixtures. Formatting and type-check jobs also pass. The 62 unchanged failures above describe the local Mac baseline, not the GitHub test result.

CI preview note: Vercel fails to resolve the Git-sourced `kicadts` package during `bun run build:site`. The upstream base commit's deployment fails with the same error; this PR does not change dependencies or the site build.

title: Preserve via connectivity after trace detour insertion
description: Fixes a bug where a route changes copper layers without an explicit via, causing crashes in the autorouting process.
body:
## Bug

Pipeline 9's SRJ18 sample 15 crashes after global repair because a route changes copper layers without an explicit via. The input to Repair03 has a valid co-located layer transition; the output does not.

`applyDrcErrorForces` collects via point indices before applying a trace repair. A terminal detour then inserts a point into the route. The later via move still uses the old indices, moves a same-layer point instead of the other end of the via, and `materializeRoutes` consequently loses that via. Subsequent errors in the same call can also reuse stale segment indices.

## Fix

- Collect current via/segment geometry for each error.
- Refresh the via point indices after segment repair, before moving the nearby via.
- Preserve terminal positions, trace widths, and both ends of every layer transition.

No DRC thresholds, solver budgets, board-name conditions, or fallbacks are changed.

## Regression test

The new small two-route/one-pad test obtains a real trace-to-via collision from `AutoroutingDrcEngine`, applies the existing repair operation, and checks connectivity. It fails before this change (one expected via becomes zero) and passes afterward. It also checks unchanged terminals and widths.

Validation: all **99 tests pass (3,647 assertions)**, including the existing snapshot tests; TypeScript and PR CI pass. A full local Pipeline 9 rerun of the previously crashing SRJ18 sample 15 now completes all **461 point-pair connections with zero benchmark DRCs**, preserving 352 physical through-vias. The [fresh same-machine comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2710#issuecomment-5808969613) confirms sample 15 no longer fails: all 16 SRJ18 scenarios complete, and 15 pass DRC. Sample 14 still has 177 DRCs in that broader integration and remains under investigation. Dataset01 passes all 85 scenarios with no outcome changes. The integration is not claimed regression-free.

This PR targets `fix/broad-repulsion-trace-pad-width`, the branch containing the Repair03 dependency commit used by autorouter PRs [#2709](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2709) and [#2710](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2710). It does not merge or replace those PRs.

title: Fix pedometer SysConfig requests and open-drain conversion

body:
After building `imrishabh18/pedometer` v1.1.3, `ti generate-sysconfig ./index.circuit.tsx` reports a missing request even though `dist/index/circuit.json` exists. The message does not explain that the missing file supplies firmware behavior. With a request supplied, the board's valid open-drain I2C declarations also fail conversion.

This change explains hardware Circuit JSON versus firmware requests, identifies missing explicit `--config` paths accurately, and supplies a tested [`index.sysconfig.json`](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/blob/fix/pedometer-sysconfig-request/docs/pedometer/index.sysconfig.json) for the current board's `U1` component and signal names. It updates the bundled converter pin to `b4458ed78fdcfeee3404af45bf30b36e06349c7d`, allowing open-drain SDA/SCL while preserving incompatible GPIO checks.

**Dependency:** merge [circuit-json-to-sysconfig #6](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/pull/6) first. The separate pre-build missing-export crash is addressed by [eval #4905](https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/pull/4905). This is a follow-up to merged #250.

Validation: 30 Node CLI tests plus the imported-component snapshot pass; formatting, typecheck, and npm package build pass. New regression tests cover missing requests after a successful TSX build, an invalid explicit request path, and open-drain I2C through the CLI. The final built npm CLI, using the committed request file and converter revision, passes both generate and real TI check on pedometer v1.1.3 with Bun 1.3.14. SysConfig 1.28.1+4785 / SimpleLink F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 generates seven files and semantic checking passes.

The example explicitly selects display isolation high, PMIC low-power low, accelerometer input, I2C at 100 kbit/s, reserved SWD pins, NoRTOS, and internal LF RCOSC. It is a configuration example, not a complete pedometer firmware application. The converter remains bundled at build time, so npm consumers do not fetch the Git dependency.

body:
Adds `ti generate-sysconfig ./pedometer.tsx` and `ti check-sysconfig ./pedometer.tsx` to the existing CLI. TSX uses the real tscircuit compiler; Circuit JSON is also accepted. An adjacent `pedometer.sysconfig.json` supplies explicit firmware choices, and stable signal names resolve through connected source traces to MCU pins. The commands require Bun on PATH.

The real pedometer run exposed a missing connected-trace lookup and two converter startup defaults. This revision fixes the lookup, forwards the explicit LF clock choice, and pins converter `9049b4cce0510088d9b48397759528cb532a0dbd` from merged [companion PR #5](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-sysconfig/pull/5) as a development dependency. The npm build bundles the converter into the CLI, so installing the published package does not fetch the GitHub dependency. That converter disables LaunchPad flash startup and requires internal LF RCOSC when DIO3/DIO4 are claimed.

`check-sysconfig` verifies the installed SDK and SysConfig versions, invokes the real TI tool, and requires nonempty driver/device C and header files. For CC2340 it also compares generated GPIO pins and states, I²C pins/rate/mux, LF clock, reserved pins, and board startup against the resolved request. For the supported AM2434 A7/B7 single-output scope, it compares the generated GPIO name, pin, direction, and MCU pinmux with the Circuit JSON request. The converter's separate real-TI runner checks byte-for-byte parity with a CCS-saved pedometer reference. The commands require Bun on PATH and fail early with a clear error when it is missing.

### Real CC2340 validation completed

- Original pedometer v0.4.4 source, compiled by tscircuit 0.0.2463; entrypoint copied byte-for-byte to `pedometer.tsx`.
- Both exact commands passed from the installed npm tarball using SysConfig **1.28.1+4785**, CCS **21.0.1**, and SimpleLink F3 SDK **9.21.00.36** at `c55fa9bae0ec71b103508afac4861d446204669b`.
- CCS opens the generated CC2340R5/RGE file and reports **no problems**. Verified GPIO20 high, GPIO3 low, GPIO12 input without pull/interrupt, SDA8/SCL6, and 100 kbit/s; internal LF RCOSC and no LaunchPad initialization.
- Real TI generated seven files. Driver C/header and device C are byte-identical to the independent reference saved through CCS. Reserved display/debug assignments and absence of LaunchPad flash routines are checked.
- Both DIO12/DIO13 fixture variants passed real TI generation. Both pedometer generated C files compile individually with TI ARM Clang 5.1.1.LTS.

[Reproduction and scope](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/blob/add-sysconfig-commands/docs/sysconfig-validation.md).

### Local validation

At head `4b0a4ae`, 27 Node CLI tests, the Bun import snapshot, root typecheck, formatting, npm bundle build, and tarball dry run pass. The 77 source tests passed on earlier head `5f9e3c8`. Tests cover the advertised input formats, explicit LF clock and Bun requirements, SDK/tool version rejection, and failures when TI's generated pin, state, I²C rate/mux, clock, reserved-pin, or startup output differs from the request. A mocked TI CLI that exits successfully with the wrong I²C rate is now rejected by `ti check-sysconfig`. AM2434 rejects malformed `reserved_ports`; CC2340 now rejects `reserved_ports: null`. New CLI/package helpers follow the handbook's named-parameter rule.

The built npm CLI generated a pedometer `.syscfg` byte-identical to the CCS-validated file. At `4b0a4ae`, the built CLI passed real `ti check-sysconfig` on the pedometer with seven generated files and on AM2434 A7/B7 with 20 files each. The AM2434 check also handles the official MCU+ SDK product metadata's trailing commas. The clean local/global tarball install passed on earlier head `eae0dca`; current-head package CI passed the clean installation and smoke tests.

### Draft status and limits

Converter PR #5 is merged. This PR remains draft and unmerged. At `4b0a4ae`, package, format-check, system-block-ui, and Vercel pass; the separate tscircuit registry build is pending. The prior registry timeout is not claimed fixed.

SysConfig 1.26.3, a complete firmware link, and hardware operation were not tested. AM2434 semantic checking remains limited to its supported single A7/B7 output GPIO; CC2340 covers the documented pedometer GPIO/I²C/clock scope. The converter's automated TI CI remains AM2434-only; CC2340 was validated locally with the dedicated runner.

title: feat: convert Altium projects with shared source identities
description: Add a staged Altium project converter that assigns stable ID scopes to PCBschematic documents and reconciles components into canonical project-wide source identities, preserving downstream PCB connectivity.
body:
## Summary

- add a staged Altium project converter, following the shared-context converter pattern used by `kicad-to-circuit-json`
- assign each PCB/schematic document a stable ID scope, then reconcile components, ports, named nets, and traces into canonical project-wide source identities
- prefer the PCB trace identity when PCB artifacts reference it, so downstream PCB connectivity is preserved
- document the project API and add a one-test-per-file PCB/schematic SVG regression

## Why

Converting documents independently and concatenating them leaves the PCB and schematic with unrelated source identities (and, before #158, colliding IDs). Downstream `circuit-json-to-tscircuit` cannot reliably reconnect PCB traces to generated TSX unless the Altium project is assembled as one semantic conversion.

This PR is stacked on #158 because document-scoped IDs are the first stage of the project converter.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/conversion/altium-project-shared-source-identities.test.ts`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- manual conversion of DRV8307EVM, LM5155EVM-FLY, LM251772EVM, and LMG342X-BB-EVM: zero duplicate primary IDs and zero PCB traces referencing missing source traces across all four projects

The full conversion suite in this fresh worktree also ran all fixture-independent tests; fixture-backed failures were only from reference downloads not being present.

title: Fix ID collisions when combining Altium documents
description: Adds an optional idPrefix to the generic, PCB, and schematic conversion APIs to prevent ID collisions when combining outputs from separate Altium documents.
body:
## Summary

- add an optional `idPrefix` to the generic, PCB, and schematic conversion APIs
- apply it in a final converter stage to every primary ID, scalar reference, and `*_ids` reference array
- document safe combination of separately converted PCB and schematic documents
- add a one-test-per-file regression that combines PCB and schematic output and verifies unique IDs, trace references, nested edge references, and Circuit JSON schema validity

## Root cause

Altium record indices are document-local. Converting a PCB and schematic separately could therefore produce the same Circuit JSON IDs (for example, both documents could emit `source_trace_altium_0`). Concatenating those outputs made downstream lookup select an unrelated element. Prefixing at the final staged-converter boundary preserves all existing converter logic while namespacing the complete output and all references consistently.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/conversion/document-scoped-circuit-json-ids.test.ts tests/architecture`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- Biome check on every changed source/test/documentation file
- `git diff --check`

The repository-wide `bun run lint` still reports pre-existing findings in files untouched by this PR; all changed files pass Biome.

title: Preserve independent oval pad and slot rotations
description: Fixes the issue where drill rotations were incorrectly applied to copper pads, ensuring independent rotations for CH582 USB mounting pads.
body:
The CH582 USB mounting pads shown in #68 have vertical drill slots inside unrotated oval copper pads. Exporting them as `pill` applied the drill rotation to the copper too, turning the mounting pads sideways.

Use the existing rounded-rectangle pad representation when the drill has an independent rotation or offset. A corner radius of half the smaller pad dimension preserves the oval copper outline without board-specific handling. Normalize relative alignment so full-turn rotations keep the existing centered `pill` representation. Non-rectangular exotic shapes retain the converter's existing oval approximation.

The CH582 USB test derives dimensions and rotations from parsed geometry and verifies independently rotated slots are present. Added centered-slot regressions for 0°, 360°, and −360° relative rotations. Geometry assertions and SVG comparisons follow the existing neighbouring SVG tests.

Refreshed the full-board and bottom-copper snapshots so both show the corrected mounting pads. An XML element comparison against main confirmed exactly four copper-pad and four drill elements changed in each snapshot; all other elements are identical. The replacement rects preserve drill positions and rotate copper separately.

Validation: GitHub CI on commit `365c826` passes the complete Bun Test workflow (8m26s), Type Check, and Format Check. Local TypeScript and Biome checks also pass. All checksum-pinned reference fixtures downloaded successfully; a redundant local full-suite run passed the conversion tests and all 57 TI schematic snapshots and was stopped during the large TI PCB render after CI completed successfully. Vercel deployment requires maintainer authorization. The PR remains Draft.

title: Accelerate bus routing while preserving clearance and route quality
description: AM3352RAM routing repeats millions of grid and collision checks. Reuse geometry-dependent work, bound collision searches, short-circuit exact clearance predicates, and use an indexed numeric queue. Equal A costs prefer progress toward the goal without weighting the heuristic; the initial compact bus envelope leaves 1 headroom before length tuning. The latest AM3352 solver measurement is 17.3 seconds on Bun 1.3.14. With the associated core scheduling and connectivity improvements, the real SVG handler takes 21.8 seconds locally, 46.9 seconds on the standard Linux CI runner, and 93.9 seconds on Vercel Standard CPU. A separately deployed Vercel Performance CPU preview takes 77.4 seconds for SVG and 71.8 seconds for Circuit JSON, with all 47 traces and zero DRC errors. The hosted 30-second target is not met by this PR. The project default was restored to Standard after the experiment. These end-to-end measurements include companion changes and are not an isolated solver speedup measurement. This version computes different routes: total planar copper improves from 1549.713 to 1528.379 mm, ordinary turns from 540 to 539, and short jogs from 145 to 138. Maximum detour changes from 2.04736 to 2.04874 (both below the tightened 2.05 bound). All 47 signals, zero errors, no acute corners, single-layer carriers, bus skew and coupled-pair gapskew checks pass. No saved geometry, board-specific route plan, relaxed clearance or reduced matching requirement is used. Unfinished search-weight, grid-resolution, and negotiation experiments are excluded. Validation: all current PR CI checks pass; the full solver suite passes; randomized queue updates and 40,000 exact-clearance equivalence checks cover the new primitives. Typecheck and package build pass. Core quality gates have been tightened to 1550 mm, 2.05 maximum detour, 540 ordinary turns and 145 short jogs. .benchmark.sh: all four DDR samples route 3333 signals with combined DRC passing and 0.100 mm total copper skew on each bus, including fixed fanouts. All 66 fixed paths per sample retain verified provenance. Local benchmark runtimes were 196 ms (bottom), 156 ms (left), 152 ms (right), and 129 ms (top). All four completed PNGs were regenerated and inspected; they are unchanged. Raw layer-mismatch samples reject as expected.

AM3352/RAM routing repeats millions of grid and collision checks. Reuse geometry-dependent work, bound collision searches, short-circuit exact clearance predicates, and use an indexed numeric queue. Equal A* costs prefer progress toward the goal without weighting the heuristic; the initial compact bus envelope leaves 1% headroom before length tuning.

The latest AM3352 solver measurement is **17.3 seconds** on Bun 1.3.14. With the associated core scheduling and connectivity improvements, the real SVG handler takes **21.8 seconds locally**, **46.9 seconds on the standard Linux CI runner**, and **93.9 seconds on Vercel Standard CPU**. A separately deployed Vercel Performance CPU preview takes **77.4 seconds** for SVG and **71.8 seconds** for Circuit JSON, with all 47 traces and zero DRC errors. **The hosted <30-second target is not met by this PR.** The project default was restored to Standard after the experiment. These end-to-end measurements include companion changes and are not an isolated solver speedup measurement. This version computes different routes: total planar copper improves from 1549.713 to 1528.379 mm, ordinary turns from 540 to 539, and short jogs from 145 to 138. Maximum detour changes from 2.04736 to 2.04874 (both below the tightened 2.05 bound). All 47 signals, zero errors, no acute corners, single-layer carriers, bus skew and coupled-pair gap/skew checks pass. No saved geometry, board-specific route plan, relaxed clearance or reduced matching requirement is used.

Unfinished search-weight, grid-resolution, and negotiation experiments are excluded.

Validation: all current PR CI checks pass; the full solver suite passes; randomized queue updates and 40,000 exact-clearance equivalence checks cover the new primitives. Typecheck and package build pass. Core quality gates have been tightened to 1550 mm, 2.05 maximum detour, 540 ordinary turns and 145 short jogs.

title: Skip redundant copper checks during dense bus routing
description: Reduces runtime by skipping unnecessary copper clearance checks for edges that cannot improve the best route during dense bus routing.
body:
Dense A* currently checks continuous copper clearance even when an edge cannot improve the best route to its destination. Reject those dominated edges before geometry work, then run hard-copper clearance only after the exact cost wins. Nonnegative soft penalties permit the early lower-bound check; negative penalties retain the existing cost path.

The grid, heuristic, tie-breaking arithmetic, search budgets, accepted-edge checks, and final DRC remain unchanged. No routing-quality constraint is relaxed.

On this ARM workstation, three runs of the AM3352 23-control stage had median runtimes of 13.62s before and 7.07s after (48% lower). The entire serialized output is identical. This measures that stage, not the full board.

Validation:
- 50 tests / 21,768 assertions pass; build, typecheck, and formatting pass.
- Four DDR benchmarks solve 132/132 connections with combined-copper DRC, immutable fanout provenance, and every bus's total-copper length-skew limit passing; each solve takes 301–440ms locally.
- All four completed DDR snapshots were regenerated, visually inspected, and remain byte-unchanged: [left→right](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_left_io_right-solved.png), [right→left](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_right_io_left-solved.png), [top→bottom](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_top_io_bottom-solved.png), [bottom→top](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_bottom_io_top-solved.png).
- Full core AM3352 passes all 169 assertions and all three original routed snapshots unchanged: 47/47 signals, native DRC, length skew, pair spacing, corner, and detour gates. On this workstation, the full reference render/validation took 251.0s before and 129.3s after (49% lower; single runs, not a cross-machine service latency guarantee). Phase timing after the change attributes about 99s to route search and 15s to matching.

Companion documentation: https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/904

title: Make bus lane routes portable across ARM and x86
description: Fixes routing discrepancies between ARM and x86 architectures by standardizing distance calculations using IEEE-754 arithmetic, ensuring consistent route generation across platforms.
body:
Equal-length AM3352 control shortcuts can choose opposite bends on ARM and x86: native `Math.hypot` differs by one ulp, and routing ranks candidates by path length. Those choices propagate through congestion negotiation into 13 different control routes and failing core snapshots.

Compute routing distances with IEEE-754 multiplication/addition and `Math.sqrt`. The reduced 23-control reproduction now produces identical routes on ARM and x86 and preserves the accepted ARM routes. Fixed fanouts and endpoints are untouched.

The regression uses the actual endpoint values that exposed the issue. It fails against the old implementation on x86 and passes with this fix on both architectures. A PR package-preview workflow builds an installable artifact for downstream core validation without releasing to npm.

Validation:
- Existing 49 solver tests plus the new regression pass; typecheck, formatting, and isolated Node/browser/TypeScript package checks pass.
- Four DDR benchmarks: 132/132 signals, combined-copper DRC, immutable fanouts, and all length-skew limits pass.
- All four completed DDR images were regenerated and visually reviewed; their files are unchanged: [left→right](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_left_io_right-solved.png), [right→left](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_right_io_left-solved.png), [top→bottom](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_top_io_bottom-solved.png), [bottom→top](docs/routed-ddr/ddr_bottom_io_top-solved.png).

[Core #4259](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4259) consumes the built preview and removes the ARM-only job. All ten regular x86 CI shards pass, including the full AM3352 routing test with its existing routed snapshots unchanged. Full AM3352 also passes on ARM with 47/47 signals and zero native errors. No snapshot tolerance or routing requirement is relaxed.

title: fix: correct release workflow YAML syntax
description: Fixes YAML parsing error in the release workflow due to incorrect scalar syntax, ensuring the workflow executes correctly without altering release behavior.
body:
Fix the release workflow failing YAML parsing before any jobs start. The colon in `chore: bump version` was inside a plain YAML scalar; make the condition a folded scalar so it is parsed as a string.

Validated both corrected workflows with Ruby YAML. Release behavior is otherwise unchanged.

title: build: publish standalone solver bundles through jscdn
description: Publish a standalone ESM package through GitHub Packages for public jscdn tarball installation, moving bundled dependencies to development dependencies and adding a GitHub Packages release workflow.
body:
Consumers currently install TypeScript source and a Git-pinned fanout dependency, pulling repository content and development artifacts into application installs. Publish a standalone ESM package through GitHub Packages for public jscdn tarball installation.

- Bundle runtime implementations and their TypeScript declarations; move bundled dependencies to development dependencies and publish only dist plus package metadata.
- Add a GitHub Packages release workflow and document the jscdn install URL. Pin TypeScript 5.9.3 for the declaration generator's compiler API.
- Check the actual tarball in CI: allowed files, a 5 MiB size budget, zero runtime/peer dependencies, isolated Node imports, browser bundling, and strict TypeScript consumption.

The unpacked release is approximately 1.13 MiB (5 files). Publishing requires merging and running the release workflow; downstream Git references can then be replaced with a versioned jscdn URL. This PR does not publish a release itself.

Validation: typecheck passed; 49 tests passed (21,765 assertions); isolated package checks passed. Benchmark: all four DDR fixtures routed 33/33 lanes with valid total-copper length matching; four raw fixtures correctly rejected for layer changes. Fixed-copper DRC reported zero errors for each completed fixture. RAM_BYTE0, RAM_BYTE1, and RAM_CA total-copper skew were each 0.1000 mm across all four fixtures. Solve times: bottom 476 ms, left 463 ms, right 451 ms, top 313 ms (wall times 544/535/516/373 ms). Solver code and fixed fanout data are unchanged; this is a packaging PR, so no routing snapshots were changed.

title: Compute clean AM3352 bus lanes without saved geometry
description: bus_lanes now computes the complete AM3352RAM layout from the original pads and constraints. The public-phase TSX regression in core 4237 passes with 4747 signals, zero native DRC errors, and no custom algorithm or saved route geometry.
body:
`bus_lanes` now computes the complete AM3352/RAM layout from the original pads and constraints. The public-phase TSX regression in [core #4237](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4237) passes with **47/47 signals, zero native DRC errors, and no custom algorithm or saved route geometry**.

![Completed AM3352 signal layers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/7affa9d1b6fff327c17f957981a300695d91a7a2/docs/routed-am3352/solved.png)

| Measurement | Generated | Reviewed reference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total planar copper | 1549.71 mm | 1696.53 mm |
| Maximum / mean detour ratio | 2.047 / 1.546 | 2.536 / 1.723 |
| Ordinary turns / short jogs | 540 / 145 | 888 / 451 |
| Acute corners | 0 | — |
| Maximum byte / pair skew | 0.635 / 0.127 mm | Within declared limits |
| Pair interior edge gap | 0.11213–0.13813 mm | 0.11979–0.13813 mm |

The reference's 6.2 mm per-end approach allowance remains unchanged. Carrier routes stay on one signal layer without vias; automatic dogbones apply only to untouched pads. Existing fanout handoffs remain fixed.

Review the pipeline in this order:
- `bus-lanes-pipeline-solver.ts`: local escapes, matched buses, then remaining controls.
- `negotiate-lanes.ts` and `select-route-candidates.ts`: generated alternatives and bounded selection, with differential pairs kept together.
- `refine-pair-approaches.ts`: clearance-checked approach tightening and legal corners after tuning-space allocation.
- `tune-coupled-lengths.ts` and `smooth-tuning.ts`: shared pair curves and rounded meanders.

Validation: 49 solver tests / 21,765 assertions; typecheck, formatting, and browser build pass. The fresh core AM3352 regression passed in about 281 seconds, including independent quality checks and native DRC. Six smaller core integration tests also pass. All three AM3352 layer views and all four existing DDR images were inspected.

`./benchmark.sh`: 4/4 DDR samples, 132/132 signals, combined-copper DRC passing, and all byte/CA skews ≤0.1 mm. Latest local solve times 346–589 ms; including validation 414–665 ms. Four incompatible-layer inputs reject as expected.

Only completed routing images are included. Dense routing remains a bounded heuristic and can take minutes or fail when routing/tuning space is insufficient. Depends on [fanout-solver #252](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/252), pinned to its tested source commit.

CI timing: the four-board integration test has an explicit 30-second timeout, and the shared-runner benchmark allows five seconds per sample while retaining every connectivity, DRC, and skew gate. The local benchmark still passes its original one-second deadline. No routing geometry or solver behavior changed in this CI fix.

title: Add a labeled 3-pin JST UART port and target connectors
description: The programmer now has a dedicated 3-pin JST SH UART port (J5) with TXGNDRX labels and 3.3 V UART1 on GPIO8GPIO9 through 100-ohm series resistors. USB exposes UART on CDC0 and preserves power telemetry on a separate CDC1 interface; changing telemetry line settings does not affect UART. Adds StandardJstUartSide and StandardJstUartUpward for target boards. Their default pin order is RXGNDTX, with each label embedded beside its corresponding footprint pad and transformed with connector placementrotation. rolehost reverses the signal labels and selectors to TXGNDRX so a straight-through cable connects host TX to target RX. Both reuse the existing verified 3-pin JST parts and CAD models. The programmer retains its original 26  42 mm outline. The power switch moves up on the left edge, and J5 UART sits below it, away from the USB-C input. Nearby resistors and the power indicator are repositioned with checked replacement routes. Packageconfig version is 0.8.0. Existing SWD, reset, power, RGB, and Tag-Connect interfaces are preserved, with checked UART routes applied afterward. The target layout examples, README previews, firmware instructions, and fabrication exporter are updated. Historical v0.7.1 fabrication archives are explicitly identified as lacking UART. Validation: All four circuit builds passed; independent routing DRC reports zero errors. TypeScript and circuit tests passed, including hosttarget pin mapping, rotated silkscreen alignment, physical copper endpoints, signal isolation, and UART via clearance from solder lands. RP2040 UF2 firmware compiled successfully against the pinned upstreamSDK commits; its actual ELF USB descriptor passed interface and endpoint collision checks. Firmware measurement math checks and fabrication export passed. Programmer and both target PCB previews were visually inspected. Hardware has not been bench-tested. The registry package has not been published.
body:
The programmer now has a dedicated 3-pin JST SH UART port (J5) with TX/GND/RX labels and 3.3 V UART1 on GPIO8/GPIO9 through 100-ohm series resistors. USB exposes UART on CDC0 and preserves power telemetry on a separate CDC1 interface; changing telemetry line settings does not affect UART.

Adds `StandardJstUartSide` and `StandardJstUartUpward` for target boards. Their default pin order is RX/GND/TX, with each label embedded beside its corresponding footprint pad and transformed with connector placement/rotation. `role="host"` reverses the signal labels and selectors to TX/GND/RX so a straight-through cable connects host TX to target RX. Both reuse the existing verified 3-pin JST parts and CAD models.

The programmer retains its original 26 × 42 mm outline. The power switch moves up on the left edge, and J5 UART sits below it, away from the USB-C input. Nearby resistors and the power indicator are repositioned with checked replacement routes. Package/config version is 0.8.0. Existing SWD, reset, power, RGB, and Tag-Connect interfaces are preserved, with checked UART routes applied afterward. The target layout examples, README previews, firmware instructions, and fabrication exporter are updated. Historical v0.7.1 fabrication archives are explicitly identified as lacking UART.

Validation:
- All four circuit builds passed; independent routing DRC reports zero errors.
- TypeScript and circuit tests passed, including host/target pin mapping, rotated silkscreen alignment, physical copper endpoints, signal isolation, and UART via clearance from solder lands.
- RP2040 UF2 firmware compiled successfully against the pinned upstream/SDK commits; its actual ELF USB descriptor passed interface and endpoint collision checks.
- Firmware measurement math checks and fabrication export passed.
- Programmer and both target PCB previews were visually inspected.

Hardware has not been bench-tested. The registry package has not been published.

title: Accept open-drain declarations on CC2340 I2C pins
description: Allows open-drain declarations for I2C SDASCL roles, resolving conflicts with existing GPIO configurations while maintaining compatibility with TIs I2CLPF3 driver.
body:
`imrishabh18/pedometer` v1.1.3 marks its MCU SDA/SCL ports as open drain. Conversion currently rejects those ports with `is_using_open_drain conflicts with requested sda function`, even though TI's I2CLPF3 driver configures both pins with `GPIO_CFG_OUT_OD_PU`.

Allow open-drain declarations for the supported SDA/SCL roles. Standard GPIO requests and contradictory push-pull/pull declarations remain rejected. Tests cover both I2C pins, output parity with undeclared electrical attributes, and contradictory settings.

Validation: 164 tests and 3 snapshots pass; formatting and typecheck pass. The regression fails before this change. The real pedometer passes `ti generate-sysconfig` and `ti check-sysconfig` using this converter, producing seven files with SysConfig 1.28.1+4785 and SimpleLink F3 SDK 9.21.00.36. The existing real-TI validator also passes GPIO/I2C settings, clock, reserved pins, exact CCS reference C/header parity, and the DIO12-to-DIO13 case.

TI driver evidence: [I2CLPF3.c at the validated SDK revision](https://github.com/TexasInstruments/simplelink-lowpower-f3-sdk/blob/c55fa9bae0ec71b103508afac4861d446204669b/source/ti/drivers/i2c/I2CLPF3.c#L725).

title: Fix CC2340 custom-board startup and validate against CCS
description: Fixes CC2340 custom-board startup issues by disabling LaunchPad-specific initialization and validating configurations against CCS, ensuring compatibility with external LF crystal selection and GPIO settings.
body:
The real pedometer TI run exposed two SDK defaults that were absent from text-only validation: external LF crystal selection conflicts with DIO3/DIO4, and LaunchPad flash shutdown drives reserved display pins. Disable LaunchPad-specific initialization for the device target and add explicit `firmware.lf_clock_source`, rejecting crystal-pin claims without `lf_rcosc`.

Add a CCS-saved reference and `bun run validate:cc2340`. Real SysConfig 1.28.1+4785 with SimpleLink F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 passed GPIO electrical/pin checks, I²C pins/mux/100-kbit/s checks, reserved display/debug checks, internal-clock checks, and both DIO12/DIO13 fixtures. The converter and independently saved CCS reference produce byte-identical `ti_drivers_config.c`, `.h`, and `ti_devices_config.c`. CCS 21.0.1 reports no problems. Both generated C files compile individually with TI ARM Clang 5.1.1.LTS.

Validation: 163 unit tests pass; typecheck and format check pass. Historical fixtures remain unchanged. The existing TI CI job is still AM2434-only; the CC2340 validation runner requires installed tools. SysConfig 1.26.3, a complete firmware link, and hardware operation are not claimed tested.

Companion dependency for tscircuit/ti#250; both remain draft pending review.
